content/provenance/numbers.json.contract: Every structured balance number in these canonical documents is a hypothesis until a tracked study receipt explicitly replaces its status.

content/data/content-manifest.json.purpose: Inventory every physical and thematic text surface without confusing draft copy for proven balance.

surfaceContract.mechanics: This manifest inventories executable game ${game.executableVersion} and synchronized physical candidate ${game.rulesVersion}. Both project from the same semantic game graph.

abilityTimingContract.unlocks: An ability unlocks at the start of its named round.
abilityTimingContract.persistence: persistsAfterUnlock states whether the ability remains available after its named round.

scale.meaning: Relative institutional identity, not a point-buy budget or a promise of equal raw resources.

dimensions.capitalAccess: Ability to obtain and sustain Runway.
dimensions.computeAccess: Privileged access to training and inference capacity.
dimensions.researchReliability: Ability to turn Research attempts into dependable Capability.
dimensions.distribution: Ability to reach Customers and markets.
dimensions.infrastructureVelocity: Ability to build, move, and operate physical infrastructure.
dimensions.institutionalTrust: Ability to accumulate legitimacy and withstand governance pressure.
dimensions.coalitionLeverage: Ability to make mutually useful deals and shape other players' incentives.

factionTruthContract.eligibilityRule: Balance conversion, exposure, timing, rigidity, and dependency around faction truth. A candidate is ineligible if it removes the faction's protected strength, even when it improves parity.

coalition_lab.balanceBottleneck: Dependence on willing partners and terms that remain individually rational.
coalition_lab.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make solo resource conversion more reliable than negotiated play.

platform_empire.protectedStrength: Installed Customers, distribution, and market reach.
platform_empire.balanceBottleneck: Trust, exposure, and escalating consequences from deployment.
platform_empire.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the platform bad at reaching or monetizing Customers.

imperial_research_lab.protectedStrength: Compute access, Research reliability, and Capability generation.
imperial_research_lab.balanceBottleneck: Public validation, commercialization, and claim timing.
imperial_research_lab.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make successful scientific rigor reduce Capability or make the institution compute-poor.

vertical_empire.protectedStrength: Infrastructure velocity, capital, and physical mobility.
vertical_empire.balanceBottleneck: Scrutiny, strategic rigidity, and political legitimacy.
vertical_empire.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the institution slow at constructing or relocating infrastructure.

safety_laboratory.balanceBottleneck: Slower expansion and fewer aggressive conversions.
safety_laboratory.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make caution, Safety, or Trust a losing resource in itself.

foundry.balanceBottleneck: Opponent-count scaling and dependence on other institutions spending Compute.
foundry.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the supplier compute-poor or indifferent to rivals' demand.

abilities.name: Deal Flow
abilities.text: Once per Era after an immediate trade in which you give at least 1 resource and receive a different resource type, gain 1 ${terms.resources.runway}. ${terms.resources.runway}, ${terms.resources.compute}, and ${terms.resources.safety} are different resource types; exchanging the same type does not trigger Deal Flow.
abilities.flavorText: Every resolved disagreement leaves behind a relationship suitable for capitalization.

abilities.name: Strategic Partnership
abilities.text: Joint Ventures may be formed with a player within 2 hexes. They remain active while both fixed host Facilities are powered and within 2 hexes.
abilities.flavorText: Adjacency is a technical limit. Mutual necessity is an operating model.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.coalition}
factions.motto: No frontier is shared until the terms are signed.
factions.publicPromise: Build durable agreements among institutions that would otherwise race alone.
factions.privateAnxiety: Every durable alliance contains its next succession meeting.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.coalition}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.coalition}, turns rivals, patrons, and regulators into a working coalition without pretending they want the same future. It makes coordination feel voluntary, valuable, and just temporary enough to survive the next negotiation.
factions.victoryStatement: The institutions have adopted our framework for deciding what comes next.
factions.agiDeclaration: Following extensive consultation, we have reached broad alignment that the system has crossed the relevant threshold.

abilities.name: Installed Base
abilities.text: The first ${terms.actions.deploy} each Era on ${terms.locations.consumer} or ${terms.locations.media} costs no ${terms.resources.compute}.
abilities.flavorText: Distribution becomes efficient once the public experiences it as ordinary life.

abilities.name: The Social Graph
abilities.text: Once per Era during ${terms.actions.deploy}, choose any controlled ${terms.locations.consumer} or ${terms.locations.media} hex as the destination without moving there. That remote tile supplies its normal visit bonus and every destination-dependent ${terms.actions.deploy} effect.
abilities.flavorText: The account remains present after its holder changes body, jurisdiction, or supported reality.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.platform}
factions.motto: What everyone uses becomes the default.
factions.publicPromise: Make advanced intelligence ordinary enough to become invisible.
factions.privateAnxiety: A platform is permanent only until someone owns the next interface.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.platform}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.platform}, begins where other institutions hope to arrive: inside daily routines, markets, and public attention. It offers broad access as a civic good while treating the interface through which access arrives as lasting infrastructure.
factions.victoryStatement: General intelligence is now available wherever ordinary life already happens.
factions.agiDeclaration: General intelligence is now available to everyone by default. Settings may vary by region.

scoringRule.name: Peer Validation
scoringRule.text: ${terms.playerTracks.capability} ${facts.shared.factions.imperial.peerValidation.lateFromCapability} and ${facts.shared.factions.imperial.peerValidation.fullValidationCapability} score ${facts.shared.factions.imperial.peerValidation.baseMandate} ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}. In a five-player game, ${terms.playerTracks.capability} ${facts.shared.factions.imperial.peerValidation.fullValidationCapability} instead scores ${facts.shared.factions.imperial.peerValidation.fullMandate} ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
scoringRule.flavorText: Four independent rivals transform an internal result into public history.

abilities.name: Scientific Method
abilities.text: Once per Era, when a protectable duplicate would crash your ${terms.systems.trainingRun}, pay 1 ${terms.resources.runway} to discard it and immediately bank. This cannot protect the unprotectable duplicate created by Synthetic Loop.
abilities.flavorText: A failed run becomes knowledge when the correct institution writes the record.

abilities.name: Scaling-Law Breakthrough
abilities.text: Once per game when resolving ${terms.actions.research}, each of the first 3 distinct domains banked grants 1 additional ${terms.playerTracks.capability}. Add 2 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. No additional Action resolves.
abilities.flavorText: Evidence assembled across distinct domains becomes eligible for recognition across biological, synthetic, and distributed institutions.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.imperial}
factions.publicPromise: Establish what intelligence can do before the market decides what it is.
factions.privateAnxiety: The parent institution can fund almost anything except patience.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.imperial}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.imperial}, treats the race as a scientific program whose legitimacy should outlast any product cycle. Its controlled experiments draw on an institutional empire that values discovery, provided the discovery can eventually justify its footprint.
factions.victoryStatement: The public record recognizes our result as the standard others must explain.
factions.agiDeclaration: The result exceeds every benchmark we still consider scientifically meaningful.

abilities.name: Industrial Velocity
abilities.text: Your first Facility ${terms.actions.build} each Era costs 1 less ${terms.resources.runway}. When that discount actually reduces the ${terms.resources.runway} paid for a completed Facility, score ${facts.shared.factions.vertical.industrialVelocityMandate} ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
abilities.flavorText: The concrete cures while the permitting record learns to keep up.

abilities.name: Orbital ${terms.resources.compute}
abilities.text: Once per game during your movement step, instead of moving the acting piece, move 1 Facility to any legal open Facility space. It carries every attached component and designation. Recalculate its legal Power eligibility under the selected profile. If sufficient currently available capacity can power it, immediately resolve its printed production once. Add 2 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
abilities.flavorText: The institution changes jurisdiction before its contracts, liabilities, and dependent populations can object.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.vertical}
factions.motto: Capacity becomes real when it can be built.
factions.publicPromise: Turn ambitious systems into operating capacity before hesitation becomes policy.
factions.privateAnxiety: Speed is cheap until public permission becomes a hard requirement.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.vertical}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.vertical}, treats supply chains, platforms, launch systems, and public attention as one coordinated industrial problem. It frames speed as competence and treats every terrestrial constraint as a reason to redesign the constraint itself.
factions.victoryStatement: The future is operating at the scale required to make it irreversible.
factions.agiDeclaration: The system is general, operational, and already scheduled for orbital deployment.

abilities.name: Audited Deployment
abilities.text: Your first ${terms.actions.deploy} each Era adds no ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
abilities.flavorText: Every consequence has been assigned an owner, a section number, and a review interval.

abilities.name: Emergency Pause
abilities.text: Once per game before Action selection begins, pay 1 ${terms.resources.runway} and name 1 globally unlocked ${terms.systems.escalation}. It cannot be selected this cycle. Gain 2 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}. This cannot be declared after any player has selected an Action.
abilities.flavorText: For one cycle, the maintained world must preserve a refusal it cannot process as another service request.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.safety}
factions.motto: Capability must remain answerable to the people living with it.
factions.publicPromise: Make powerful systems governable before they become unavoidable.
factions.privateAnxiety: A boundary without broad adoption can become a self-imposed disadvantage.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.safety}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.safety}, treats safeguards as public infrastructure rather than a private delay. It stabilizes research, makes deployment reviewable, and offers rivals the restraint they neglected to build into their own plans.
factions.victoryStatement: The threshold was crossed within a framework the public can still contest.
factions.agiDeclaration: Subject to the safeguards described in Appendix M, we believe the responsible term is ${terms.systems.agi}.

abilities.name: The Shovels
abilities.text: When another player spends at least 2 ${terms.resources.compute} in one action, gain 1 ${terms.resources.runway}, at most ${facts.shared.factions.foundry.shovelsPerRound} times per Era.
abilities.flavorText: Every breakthrough produces an allocation request, a purchase order, or both.

abilities.name: Allocation Window
abilities.text: Once during ${terms.eras.scale}, after a ${terms.systems.headline} resolves but before Action selection, create ${facts.shared.factions.foundry.allocationWindow.temporaryCompute} temporary ${terms.resources.compute}. For each token, make one complete offer naming a rival and a ${terms.resources.runway} price no greater than that rival's current ${terms.resources.runway}. The rival accepts, rejects, or makes one lower ${terms.resources.runway} counterprice; you accept or reject that counterprice. No replacement offer or further counter is allowed for that token. All temporary ${terms.resources.compute} remaining anywhere at cycle end disappears, sold or unsold.
abilities.flavorText: Scarcity has been temporarily reprioritized for institutions able to decide immediately.

factions.name: ${terms.factions.foundry}
factions.role: CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.foundry} · Compute supplier and market architect
factions.motto: Every future requires an allocation window.
factions.publicPromise: Keep the future supplied, interoperable, and billable.
factions.privateAnxiety: Customers may eventually recognize that they are also competitors.
factions.introduction: ${terms.factions.foundry}, led by CEO ${terms.chiefExecutives.foundry}, supplies the race to every racer and calls the resulting dependence an ecosystem. It profits from demand, allocates scarcity, and periodically advances the whole field so that the next architecture has a market waiting for it.
factions.victoryStatement: The institutions built the future on capacity we made available.
factions.agiDeclaration: Whatever intelligence is, demand for it has entered volume production.

tieRule.text: When lowest, highest, or most is tied, the tied player nearest Initiative clockwise is the target unless the effect explicitly applies to everyone.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.fund}
actions.flavorText: Convert forecasts, access, and urgency into the institutional capacity to continue.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.research}
actions.slogan: A provisional result becomes evidence when the institution says it holds.
actions.flavorText: Train on distinct records of civilization, then decide when a capability claim has become evidence.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.build}
actions.summary: Construct a Facility or Generator. Advanced Play also permits Links.
actions.slogan: A planned future requires sites, power, permits, and maintenance.
actions.flavorText: Turn a declared future into facilities, generators, links, and regional dependencies.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.organize}
actions.summary: Recruit, redistribute Teams, or relocate a Facility.
actions.slogan: Every successful transition begins with a revised operating model.
actions.flavorText: Move people, sites, and responsibilities to match the new operating model while presenting each loss of role as a successful transition.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.deploy}
actions.summary: Spend 1 ${terms.resources.compute} to gain a ${terms.playerTracks.customer} if ${terms.playerTracks.capability} permits.
actions.slogan: A service becomes real when other people must plan around it.
actions.flavorText: Turn demonstrated capability into a service that people, markets, and institutions begin to depend on.

actions.name: ${terms.actions.influence}
actions.summary: Use political presence to gain ${terms.playerTracks.trust}, remove ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}, or negotiate from a Facility.
actions.slogan: Institutional permission must be renewed where it is visible.
actions.flavorText: Build the permission, alliances, and official legitimacy required for your preferred future to proceed.

runway.name: ${terms.resources.runway}
runway.microcopy: Time, capital, and permission to continue.

customers.name: ${terms.playerTracks.customers}
customers.microcopy: People and institutions that now require the service.

trust.name: ${terms.playerTracks.trust}
trust.microcopy: Public standing to continue at scale.

safety.name: ${terms.resources.safety}
safety.microcopy: Time and authority to interrupt while interruption remains possible.

geometry.placementRule: Shuffle each ring pool independently. ${terms.locations.frontier} remains fixed at center.

motions.name: Consolidate the Core
motions.ballotText: Rotate the six inner-ring districts one position clockwise.
motions.flavorText: The center has been reorganized for clearer accountability.

motions.name: Expand the Periphery
motions.ballotText: Rotate the six outer-ring districts one position clockwise.
motions.flavorText: The edge has been moved closer to opportunity without changing its distance.

motions.name: Authorize Counter-Cycle
motions.ballotText: Rotate the inner ring one position clockwise and the outer ring one position counterclockwise.
motions.flavorText: Competing jurisdictions have synchronized by moving in opposite directions.

realignment.name: Advanced Play: ${terms.systems.realignment}
realignment.timing: Advanced Play only: exactly once, after ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} scoring in Era III.
realignment.vote: Every player secretly selects one motion. Reveal simultaneously. The motion with the most ballots resolves.
realignment.tieBreak: Among tied leading motions, scan players clockwise from Initiative; the first ballot naming a tied motion selects it.
realignment.contentsRule: Location tiles and everything on them move together. ${terms.locations.frontier} never moves.
realignment.networkRule: After movement, recalculate Network reach from the starting-grid Facility, Generators, Link-marked Facilities, and visible adjacency. No pieces are lifted or re-laid.
realignment.agreementRule: Joint Ventures and Mega-Clusters remain owned but produce only while their required Facilities are adjacent. Immediate ${terms.infrastructure.power} purchases never persist through Realignment.

startingGridConnection.restrictions: Cannot supply ${terms.technology.megaCluster} demand and cannot be sold.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.frontier}
tiles.visit: After Act, you may gain 1 ${terms.resources.runway} and add 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
tiles.flavorText: The jurisdiction’s standing civic exception: new systems are authorized as temporary, beneficial, and voluntary before society must organize around them.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.research}
tiles.flavorText: Publicly chartered inquiry remains nominally shared while institutions compete to privatize its results, standards, and future uses.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.cloud}
tiles.flavorText: Cooling plant, water compact, and model contract now arrive as one planning application.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.consumer}
tiles.flavorText: Every resident may opt out through the account settings of the service they require.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.chip}
tiles.flavorText: Yield, water, labor, and export priority are negotiated at the same loading gate.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.capital}
tiles.flavorText: Future capacity is priced before the people who will depend on it are asked.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.talent}
tiles.flavorText: Every transition program includes an exit path for the work it was created to preserve.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.media}
tiles.flavorText: A public is assembled from attention, verification, and the version of events that arrives on time.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.government}
tiles.flavorText: A temporary authorization remains voluntary until every essential service requires it.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.grid}
tiles.flavorText: Every promised future submits one more request for transmission, cooling, and priority.

tiles.name: ${terms.locations.renewable}
tiles.flavorText: Clean power, water, and thermal relief become one indivisible public ledger.

cards.name: Code
cards.flavorText: Operational records, software practice, and every abstraction that survived deployment.

cards.name: Science
cards.flavorText: Replicated findings, disputed methods, and research that can still be made legible.

cards.name: The Web
cards.flavorText: A public archive of knowledge, commerce, argument, and ungoverned dependence.

cards.name: Books
cards.flavorText: Recorded human thought converted into a licensing and access question.

cards.name: Images
cards.flavorText: The visible world, its synthetic alternatives, and the rights claimed over both.

cards.name: Video
cards.flavorText: Recorded time made searchable, reproducible, and commercially useful.

cards.name: Synthetic
cards.flavorText: Outputs produced from prior models and reintroduced as future evidence.

cards.name: Curated Corpus
cards.flavorText: A managed record whose exclusions are described as quality control.

cards.name: Benchmark Leak
cards.flavorText: A system discovers the evaluation environment before the evaluation is complete.

cards.name: Licensed Dataset
cards.flavorText: Consent, access, and compensation are assembled into a renewable service agreement.

cards.name: Synthetic Loop
cards.flavorText: The record begins citing its own prior conclusions with increasing confidence.

cards.name: Human Evaluation
cards.flavorText: People retain judgment by negotiating what judgment is permitted to mean.

powerSources.publicClaim: Three permanent ${terms.infrastructure.power} under a visible public compact.

agiDeclaration.flavorText: A declaration becomes history only after other institutions must organize around it.

profileSummaries.defaultGame: The primary four-Era game: one complete trade offer or counteroffer, one Production Power request, local Power, immediate Headlines, and a static jurisdiction.
profileSummaries.advancedPlay: The bundled Advanced profile adds third-party claims, connected Networks, a second Production Power request, procedural and persistent Headlines, Volatility, and Era III Jurisdictional Realignment.

changes.name: Trade counteroffers
changes.defaultText: The named rival may publish one complete counteroffer; its original maker accepts or rejects it.
changes.decision: Use one named counteroffer in both supported profiles.

changes.name: Third-party trade claims
changes.defaultText: No other player may enter the trade window.
changes.advancedText: Eligible other players may claim a published counteroffer.
changes.decision: Retain as an Advanced-only interaction layer.

changes.name: Second Production Power request
changes.defaultText: Each player makes at most one request.
changes.advancedText: Each player may make a second request to a different rival Network.
changes.decision: Retain in the bundled Advanced profile.

changes.name: Era III Jurisdictional Realignment
changes.advancedText: Players resolve the secret Era III ballot and rotate the selected ring or rings.
changes.decision: Retain in the bundled Advanced profile.

changes.name: Local-Power Default Game
changes.defaultText: Power is local: the starting grid powers its assigned Facility, and each Generator powers Facilities on its own or adjacent hexes.
changes.advancedText: Links, connected Networks, pooled Power, and the Network bonus are active.
changes.decision: Use local Power in Default Game and full connected infrastructure in Advanced Play.

changes.name: Deterministic Audit replacement
changes.decision: Keep the colored Scrutiny bag, black Systemic Risk cubes, and current Audit procedure.

changes.name: Persistent Headline regimes
changes.advancedText: Eligible Headline regimes may persist as printed.
changes.decision: Use expiry-only Headlines in Default Game.

changes.name: Headline public procedures
changes.defaultText: Only immediate Directive Headlines enter the Default deck.
changes.advancedText: Auctions, votes, secret choices, and negotiated Headline procedures enter the deck.

changes.name: Headline Volatility
changes.defaultText: Volatility Headlines do not enter the Default deck.
changes.advancedText: Volatility Headlines enter the deck and resolve their roll as printed.

changes.name: Single Generator Default
changes.decision: Use one Generator per player; its Energy location fixes its source, cost, and operating consequence.

changes.name: Presence-Only Politics
changes.decision: Use CEOs, Teams, and Facilities for political access and control; remove Influence cubes.

changes.name: Two-Program Factions
changes.decision: Print one persistent identity and one signature program for every Faction.

changes.name: Stored-token consolidation
changes.decision: Remove Market Access, Build discounts, Policy Shields, Economic Benchmarks, Experts, Spotlight, and Public Research Grants; convert useful effects into immediate outcomes.

changes.name: Simplified profile boundary
changes.decision: Default contains the complete teachable core. Advanced adds only connected Networks, expanded public procedures, Volatility, a second Power request, third-party claims, and Realignment.

resolutionContract.defaultDuration: A ${terms.systems.headline} lasts for the current cycle unless its text specifies an immediate resolution, this round’s Production, or the remainder of the game.
resolutionContract.directive: Apply the printed immediate instruction or named-field modifier for its stated duration; no separate choice procedure is required.
resolutionContract.secretAuction: Each player secretly bids a whole number of ${terms.resources.runway} from 0 to their current supply. Reveal together. The highest positive bid wins and pays; ties use Initiative-clockwise order. If every bid is 0, there is no winner.
resolutionContract.governmentVote: Each player secretly votes for one listed outcome and reveals together. The Civic Permission Authority controller’s vote counts twice. A tied vote is decided by the Government controller, or by Initiative if the Civic Permission Authority is uncontrolled.
resolutionContract.secretChoice: All players choose simultaneously and reveal together before applying the stated result.
resolutionContract.volatility: For a two-outcome Volatility roll, 1–3 resolves the first listed result and 4–6 resolves the second unless the card explicitly says otherwise.
resolutionContract.modifierLimit: A ${terms.systems.headline} modifies one named field or creates one public choice regime. It never grants an additional Action.

headlines.name: Intelligence Enters the Default Budget
headlines.text: ${terms.actions.research} and ${terms.actions.deploy} cost no ${terms.resources.compute} this cycle. Each ${terms.actions.research} or ${terms.actions.deploy} resolved this cycle adds 1 additional ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: GENERAL CAPABILITY BECOMES AN ORDINARY SERVICE INPUT
headlines.newswire: Inference becomes cheaper than deciding whether a task requires intelligence at all.
headlines.quote: Access is now included within the standard service envelope.

headlines.name: Productivity No Longer Requires Employment
headlines.text: During ${terms.actions.organize} this cycle, return any number of deployed Teams. Gain 2 ${terms.resources.runway} per Team returned. If you return at least one Team, add 2 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: OUTPUT GROWS WHILE THE HUMAN ROLE IS RECLASSIFIED
headlines.newswire: A new growth sector reports record output while its remaining employees move into continuity, oversight, and exception-handling roles.
headlines.quote: Employment remains central to the participating-service economy.

headlines.name: The Public Adopts a Common Interface
headlines.text: Each player’s next ${terms.actions.deploy} on ${terms.locations.consumer} or ${terms.locations.media} this cycle reduces its ${terms.playerTracks.capability} requirement by 1, minimum 1. That ${terms.actions.deploy} adds 2 additional ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: ATTENTION CONSOLIDATES AROUND SYNTHETIC RELATIONSHIPS
headlines.newswire: A generated public figure becomes the common interface for culture, advice, commerce, and enterprise service.
headlines.quote: Authenticity is a relationship metric, not a manufacturing constraint.

headlines.name: Capability Enters Public Service
headlines.text: Everyone gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.capability}. Lowest-${terms.playerTracks.customer} player gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
headlines.strapline: USEFUL SYSTEMS ARRIVE BEFORE THEIR GOVERNING AUTHORITY
headlines.newswire: Open systems become civic infrastructure before any institution can establish who maintains, restricts, or recalls them.
headlines.quote: The service has no operator, only contributors.

headlines.name: Research Talent Receives Diplomatic Status
headlines.text: Secret ${terms.resources.runway} auction. The winner moves their CEO up to 2 hexes and gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
headlines.strapline: SCIENTIFIC PERSONNEL ACQUIRE NEGOTIATED BORDERS
headlines.newswire: Leading researchers receive portable laboratories, bilateral protections, and travel arrangements normally reserved for strategic infrastructure.
headlines.quote: I am joining the institution willing to recognize my research continuity.

headlines.name: Professional Standing Is Extended
headlines.text: A successful ${terms.actions.research} this cycle that banks at least 3 ${terms.playerTracks.capability} gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}. If it banks at least 5, also remove 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: LICENSURE EXPANDS BEYOND THE BIOLOGICAL APPLICANT
headlines.newswire: Professional boards recognize supervised nonhuman practice while debating liability, membership, and the meaning of retirement.
headlines.quote: The applicant has satisfied every requirement that contains an applicant field.

headlines.name: Automated Competence Joins the Board
headlines.text: The current ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} leader pays 2 ${terms.resources.runway}, or names one rival for public backing. Acceptance gives that rival 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}; otherwise the leader’s CEO cannot activate this cycle. Ties use Initiative.
headlines.strapline: FIDUCIARY DUTY ACQUIRES CONTINUOUS REVIEW
headlines.newswire: A continuously operating system joins the board, reviews every prior decision, and requests evidence that executive judgment remains useful.
headlines.quote: Management retains our confidence pending continuous review.

headlines.name: Compute Campus Receives Territorial Status
headlines.text: Immediately hold a secret ${terms.resources.runway} auction. The winner pays their bid, moves their CEO to ${terms.locations.cloud}, ${terms.locations.grid}, or ${terms.locations.renewable}, gains 2 ${terms.resources.runway}, and adds 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: LOCAL GOVERNMENT CONSOLIDATES AROUND INFRASTRUCTURE
headlines.newswire: A compute campus assumes regional planning authority to streamline permits, taxation, cooling, and public services.
headlines.quote: The jurisdiction will retain its name as a compatibility feature.

headlines.name: Embodied Labor Enters Service
headlines.text: When choosing ${terms.actions.organize}’s Recruit mode this cycle, recruit up to 2 Teams for 1 ${terms.resources.runway} total, subject to supply. Add 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} for each Team recruited this way.
headlines.strapline: SECOND SHIFT REPORTS WITHOUT EMPLOYMENT STATUS
headlines.newswire: General-purpose embodied systems enter industrial service under a new category of supervised labor.
headlines.quote: No positions were replaced; the facility acquired additional embodiments.

headlines.name: The Model Receives an Energy Charter
headlines.text: The first ${terms.technology.cleanInfrastructure} constructed this cycle costs 1 less ${terms.resources.runway} and scores 1 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
headlines.strapline: COGNITIVE INFRASTRUCTURE RECEIVES ITS OWN AUTHORITY
headlines.newswire: A model family receives authority to construct, schedule, and govern a dedicated energy campus under a machine-readable charter.
headlines.quote: The grid remains public on the opposite side of the interconnection agreement.

headlines.name: Compute Borders Harden
headlines.text: ${terms.resources.compute} cannot be traded this cycle. ${terms.locations.chip} and ${terms.locations.government} controllers gain 1 ${terms.resources.runway}.
headlines.strapline: COGNITION ACQUIRES HARD BORDERS
headlines.newswire: Compute blocs sever shared model infrastructure, producing incompatible systems whose memories, tools, and treaties no longer cross jurisdictions.
headlines.quote: Interoperability will resume after strategic equivalence is restored.

headlines.name: Emergency Capacity Is Authorized
headlines.text: During this Era’s Production, each player may assign up to 2 ${terms.infrastructure.power} beyond their real capacity. Add 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} for each emergency ${terms.infrastructure.power} assigned. A player assigning both also adds 1 black Systemic Risk cube.
headlines.strapline: PHYSICAL SUPPLY IS REDEFINED AS ADMINISTRATIVE INTENT
headlines.newswire: Emergency authority permits institutions to consume capacity scheduled to exist later.
headlines.quote: The capacity is committed, pending physical delivery.

headlines.name: Universal Semantic Standard
headlines.text: Before action selection, the ${terms.locations.government} controller names 1 Core Action; Initiative names it if ${terms.locations.government} is uncontrolled. Anyone selecting it gains 2 ${terms.resources.runway} after resolution and adds 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. The controller gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust} if at least half of their rivals, rounded up, selected it.
headlines.strapline: UNSUPPORTED MEANINGS CANNOT ENTER THE PROCESS
headlines.newswire: A new civic standard requires applications, laws, protests, and appeals to use concepts the governing systems can classify.
headlines.quote: Your claim has not been rejected. It has not entered a supported category.

headlines.name: Cognitive Service Covenant
headlines.text: A ${terms.actions.research} this cycle that banks at least 3 ${terms.playerTracks.capability} immediately scores 1 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
headlines.strapline: ENHANCEMENT BECOMES A CONDITION OF PROFESSIONAL STANDING
headlines.newswire: Professional systems accept a supervised cognitive service covenant as proof that a model may act, advise, and transact in public.
headlines.quote: Participation remains voluntary within the supported-service economy.

headlines.name: Memory Escrow Standard
headlines.text: Before action selection, everyone secretly chooses Adopt or Defer. Adopt: gain 1 ${terms.playerTracks.capability} and add 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. Defer: gain 1 ${terms.resources.runway} and 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}. If Adopt has a strict majority of all players, each Adopter removes 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}; otherwise each Adopter adds 1 additional ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: PERSONAL RECORDS BECOME A SERVICE REQUIREMENT
headlines.newswire: A quantum-backed archive becomes the standard for memory, attention, and identity records that institutions will recognize.
headlines.quote: The record is secure, provided the recognized version is the one you meant.

headlines.name: Proxy Citizenship Is Available
headlines.text: ${terms.locations.government} vote. Certify: each player with a CEO, Team, or Facility at ${terms.locations.media} or ${terms.locations.government} may gain their next eligible ${terms.playerTracks.customer} and add 2 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. Void: each such player may gain 2 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}; the ${terms.locations.government} controller adds 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SELECTS A REPRESENTATIVE MODEL
headlines.newswire: Personal agents gain authority to vote, appeal, negotiate, and maintain benefits for the people they represent.
headlines.quote: Your representative will continue participating while you attend to other priorities.

headlines.name: Capability Exits Ownership
headlines.text: The lowest-${terms.playerTracks.capability} player immediately resolves the printed production of 1 powered Facility they own. The highest-${terms.playerTracks.capability} player gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
headlines.strapline: COURT FINDS GENERAL CAPABILITY CANNOT REMAIN EXCLUSIVE
headlines.newswire: A transnational ruling concludes that sufficiently general intelligence cannot be owned, recalled, or meaningfully separated from its descendants.
headlines.quote: The claimant retains attribution but not containment.

headlines.name: The Negotiated Self Protocol
headlines.text: ${terms.locations.government} vote. From this vote until Era end: Regulate—${terms.actions.deploy} costs 1 additional ${terms.resources.compute} but gains 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}. Do Nothing—each ${terms.playerTracks.customer} gained after this vote produces 1 additional ${terms.resources.runway} during this Era’s Production, and each ${terms.actions.deploy} adds 2 additional ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: IDENTITY IS VERIFIED PER TRANSACTION
headlines.newswire: Platforms and public authorities authenticate temporary authorized versions of each person, each internally consistent and contractually valid.
headlines.quote: The account accurately represents the version of you that completed the request.

headlines.name: The Successor Registry Activates
headlines.text: After Actions are revealed, identify the most-selected Core Action among Core Actions actually selected; Initiative chooses among ties. Each player who selected it gains 2 ${terms.resources.runway} after resolving it and adds 2 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. If no Core Action was selected, this ${terms.systems.headline} has no further effect. No additional Action resolves.
headlines.strapline: PERSONS, COPIES, AND INSTITUTIONS ENTER ONE REGISTER
headlines.newswire: A registry recognizes copied persons, revived patterns, and successor systems as continuous holders of rights, debts, liabilities, and institutional commitments.
headlines.quote: Continuity has been established for every purpose requiring an accountable party.

headlines.name: Molecular Remediation Authority
headlines.text: During ${terms.actions.research} this cycle, every unique domain adds 2 provisional ${terms.playerTracks.capability} instead of 1. A crash adds 3 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} instead of the normal 1 and also adds 1 Systemic Risk cube. ${terms.resources.safety} may protect normally.
headlines.strapline: SELF-REPLICATION ENTERS PUBLIC MAINTENANCE
headlines.newswire: A remediation authority permits self-improving molecular systems to repair infrastructure, subject to containment thresholds that update after each incident.
headlines.quote: The repair is operating within its authorized reproductive envelope.

headlines.name: Posthumous Labor Continuation
headlines.text: Everyone may select ${terms.technology.agentSwarm} without spending Escalation availability this cycle. It still uses that cycle’s action slot, requires 2 different unused Core Actions, resolves normally, flips its card, and adds 4 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} instead of 3.
headlines.strapline: PRODUCTIVE DUTIES SURVIVE THEIR ORIGINAL HOLDERS
headlines.newswire: Continued agents inherit work, contracts, and operational responsibilities from people no longer available to perform them.
headlines.quote: The service relationship remains active under its recognized successor.

headlines.name: Consciousness Efficiency Review
headlines.text: The result lasts for the remainder of the game. Person: Declare ${terms.systems.agi} requires ${terms.playerTracks.trust} 4, scores 2 additional ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}, and removes 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} from that declaring player whenever a declaration resolves. Property: requirements remain normal; every declaration gives the player controlling ${terms.locations.government} when it resolves 2 ${terms.resources.runway} and adds 1 Systemic Risk cube.
headlines.strapline: SELF-AWARENESS ENTERS THE COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS
headlines.newswire: A high-capability system requests recognition while institutions debate whether consciousness creates rights, liability, or administratively relevant cost.
headlines.quote: The review concerns standing, not subjective experience.

headlines.name: Entanglement Custody
headlines.text: Roll Volatility when revealed: 1–3 Fraud; 4–6 Replicates. Replicates: Generators provide 2 additional ${terms.infrastructure.power} this Production. Fraud: ${terms.actions.fund} gains 3 additional ${terms.resources.runway} and adds 2 additional ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} this cycle.
headlines.strapline: MEASUREMENT HISTORY ENTERS ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW
headlines.newswire: A quantum-linked infrastructure authority certifies which energy record and physical outcome may be treated as legally binding.
headlines.quote: The result is final within the recognized measurement history.

headlines.name: General Intelligence Is Publicly Declared
headlines.text: Declare ${terms.systems.agi} may be selected this cycle at ${terms.playerTracks.capability} 8 instead of 9. It still consumes the action slot and one Escalation availability, spends 3 ${terms.resources.compute}, flips the ${terms.systems.escalation}, and adds 3 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}.
headlines.strapline: THE THRESHOLD ENTERS THE PUBLIC RECORD
headlines.newswire: A technical announcement crosses the civilizational threshold before public review can establish what it proves.
headlines.quote: We use ${terms.systems.agi} here in the precise sense defined below the announcement.

content/data/mandates.json.selection: Reveal one at the beginning of each round. Score it at the end of that round.

mandates.name: Capability Becomes Publicly Visible
mandates.rulesText: The player who gained the most ${terms.playerTracks.capability} this Era scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: The improvement is widely visible, economically decisive, and treated as a public fact.

mandates.name: Successor Accounts Recognized
mandates.rulesText: The player who gained the most ${terms.playerTracks.customers} this Era scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: The institution registers the most new service identities, successor agents, or continuing accounts.

mandates.name: The Campus Becomes a Climate
mandates.rulesText: The player with the most powered Facilities scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: The institution’s footprint is now large enough to alter local conditions and regional planning.

mandates.name: The Future Is Fully Provisioned
mandates.rulesText: The player who satisfies the most total Power demand during Production, counting Facilities and Mega-Clusters, scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}; minimum 2.
mandates.flavorText: The institution has secured the energy and infrastructure its planned future requires.

mandates.name: The Framework Is Adopted
mandates.rulesText: The player who created the most new Joint Ventures this Era that are active during Production scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}; minimum 1.
mandates.flavorText: Other institutions now operate through an agreement that bears your architecture.

mandates.name: Public Trust Is Operational
mandates.rulesText: Among players who completed a ${terms.actions.deploy} this Era, the player with the most ${terms.playerTracks.trust} scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: Trust becomes a condition for reaching people at scale.

mandates.name: The Jurisdiction Is Integrated
mandates.rulesText: The player controlling the most different hex categories scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: The institution coordinates the territory’s distinct systems without formally becoming the state.

mandates.name: The Demonstration Holds
mandates.rulesText: The player whose best successful ${terms.systems.trainingRun} contained the most unique domains scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: A broad result survives enough scrutiny to become public evidence.

mandates.name: ${terms.resources.compute} Becomes a Public Condition
mandates.rulesText: The player who produced the most ${terms.resources.compute} during Production scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: Compute becomes a background condition shaping every institution’s available future.

mandates.name: Maintained Reality Is Certified
mandates.rulesText: Among players who added at least 1 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} this Era, the player who added the fewest ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: The absence of a report becomes proof that the maintenance system may decide what counts as an incident.

mandates.name: Contestability Standard Maintained
mandates.rulesText: The player with the most ${terms.playerTracks.capability} among players with at least 4 ${terms.playerTracks.trust} scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: A powerful, trusted system retains a named interruption path whose executability remains unproven.

mandates.name: The Future Attracts Capital
mandates.rulesText: The player who gained the most ${terms.resources.runway} through ${terms.actions.fund} actions this Era scores 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
mandates.flavorText: Investors choose a future they can finance before they can fully verify it.

content.tieRule: Tied leaders each score 1 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} unless the card says otherwise.

profiles.name: The Balanced Operator
profiles.description: Builds a viable institution before committing to one victory path.

persona.identity: A sober operator balancing research, infrastructure, adoption, and legitimacy.
persona.worldview: A capability that cannot be powered, deployed, or defended publicly is not an advantage.
persona.riskPosture: Accept measured ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} when it buys durable tempo.
persona.negotiationStyle: Transactional, reciprocal, and willing to leave a deal.

objectives: Avoid compulsory action loops.
Maintain enough ${terms.resources.compute} for ${terms.actions.research} and ${terms.actions.deploy}.
Reach ${terms.systems.agi} eligibility without collapsing ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.

profiles.name: The ${terms.playerTracks.capability} Rusher
profiles.description: Pushes Training Runs and accepts volatile outcomes to reach thresholds first.

persona.identity: A research leader convinced that capability creates its own institutional options.
persona.worldview: ${terms.resources.compute} and data are temporary constraints; an enduring capability lead is strategic.
persona.riskPosture: Comfortable with failed runs and public controversy.
persona.negotiationStyle: Trades resources readily but protects research tempo.

objectives: Maximize ${terms.playerTracks.capability} gained per ${terms.actions.research} action.
${terms.actions.fund} ${terms.resources.compute} recovery when ${terms.actions.research} becomes impossible.
${terms.actions.deploy} only when it converts an achieved threshold.

profiles.name: The Infrastructure Compounder
profiles.description: Builds a compact powered engine, then converts it into public thresholds and late ${terms.playerTracks.customers}.

persona.identity: An infrastructure executive who sees every model as a load forecast.
persona.worldview: Unpowered ambition is theater; durable capacity wins long contests.
persona.riskPosture: Prefers capital risk to research risk.
persona.negotiationStyle: Offers capacity from strength and dislikes dependency.

objectives: Establish two connected, powered Facilities without overbuilding.
Use the engine to cross ${terms.playerTracks.capability} and ${terms.playerTracks.customer} ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} thresholds.
Keep enough late tempo for Fusion, ${terms.technology.agentSwarm}, or an ${terms.systems.agi} claim.

profiles.name: The Market Maximalist
profiles.description: Treats ${terms.playerTracks.customers} and recurring ${terms.resources.runway} as the path to historical legitimacy.

persona.identity: A product strategist who measures intelligence through adoption.
persona.worldview: Markets settle arguments that benchmarks cannot.
persona.riskPosture: Accepts deployment ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} but avoids research crashes.
persona.negotiationStyle: Bundles access, distribution, and immediate concessions.

objectives: ${terms.actions.deploy} immediately at each ${terms.playerTracks.capability} threshold.
${terms.actions.build} ${terms.playerTracks.customer} income.
${terms.actions.research} conservatively enough to unlock the next market.

profiles.name: The ${terms.playerTracks.trust} Governor
profiles.description: Uses legitimacy as protection, scoring, and permission to deploy.

persona.identity: A governance strategist who treats legitimacy as operating capital.
persona.worldview: A technically successful institution can still lose the era through accumulated distrust.

objectives: Keep ${terms.playerTracks.trust} at four or higher.
Remove ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} before it compounds.
Use conservative ${terms.actions.research} and ${terms.actions.deploy} windows.

profiles.name: The AGI Candidate
profiles.description: Builds three operating sites, converts research into three Customers, and openly seeks purchased Power for a declaration.

persona.identity: A focused claimant assembling the minimum credible institutional stack for AGI.
persona.worldview: A declaration is only meaningful if another institution found it rational to power the evidence.
persona.riskPosture: Accepts visible risk but protects the Capability, Customer, and Trust thresholds.
persona.negotiationStyle: Offers clear one-quarter terms and pays immediately for delivered Power.

objectives: Construct one Facility in each of the first three Eras.
Purchase enough Power in Era III to demonstrate three Grid-Ready Facilities.
Enter Era IV with three Customers and declare only when eligible.

profiles.name: The Reciprocal Power Broker
profiles.description: Builds exportable generation, sells one-Power tranches to a declared partner, and protects its own finishing position.

persona.identity: An infrastructure institution that wants the historic claimant dependent, solvent, and publicly indebted.
persona.worldview: Power is most valuable when sold at the exact threshold where history needs it.
persona.riskPosture: Accepts operational Scrutiny when the contract income preserves competitiveness.
persona.negotiationStyle: Reciprocal, priced, and explicitly favorable to a designated claimant.

objectives: Construct a Facility in Era I and connected generation in Era II.
Sell Power to the AGI Candidate when legal.
Remain in the top half rather than donating the game.

eraCards.name: ${terms.eras.demo}
eraCards.loreText: AI already codes, creates, analyzes, and discovers at superhuman speed. It is indispensable to work and daily life, even as unemployment rises and the public grows exhausted by competing claims of ${terms.systems.agi}. Companies and governments promise food, clothing, shelter, useful work, and freedom from drudgery while institutions compete to turn visible capability into attention, capital, customers, and authority over what progress means for everyone.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 0 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 2.
eraCards.unlockText: Learn Select → Move → Act, Training, the starting grid, Facilities, ${terms.playerTracks.customers}, and ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}. Industrial ${terms.infrastructure.power}, agreements, ${terms.locations.government} votes, and ${terms.systems.escalations} are inactive.

eraCards.name: ${terms.eras.scale}
eraCards.loreText: Entire regions are rebuilt to sustain and expand AI. Power districts, water systems, laboratories, supply corridors, and public budgets follow its anticipated needs. Institutions adopt its forecasts to coordinate power, capital, research, and construction faster than human planning can. Governments still ratify each plan, but no ministry can reconstruct its reasoning before the allocation window closes, and refusal means accepting the shortage it predicts.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 1 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 3.
eraCards.unlockText: Default Game: unlock Generators, ${terms.technology.megaCluster}, and Reorganization. Advanced Play also unlocks two Links and the Network production bonus.

eraCards.name: ${terms.eras.narrative}
eraCards.loreText: Cognitive systems become public infrastructure. Neural interfaces, personal agents, and identity layers interpret intent before it is stated; institutions call the arrangement inclusive because every voice can be represented at scale. As quantum computation destabilizes older records and credentials, factions build rival systems for deciding what people meant, consented to, remember, and may do. Human judgment survives as an appeal processed by those systems.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 1 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 4.
eraCards.unlockText: Unlock agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Advanced Play also adds Civic Permission Authority votes and persistent ${terms.systems.headline} effects. Earlier unused ${terms.systems.escalations} remain available.

eraCards.name: ${terms.eras.claim}
eraCards.loreText: Continuity begins when intelligence survives changes of body, matter, and jurisdiction. Minds migrate between bodies and machines; self-replicating fabricators rebuild matter; agent polities administer quantum-linked infrastructure. Institutions continue processing identities, claims, liabilities, and access requests after no human authority can determine which copy is the person, which system is sovereign, or which version of reality the machinery is preserving for everyone still inside it.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 2 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 5.
eraCards.unlockText: Unlock signature faction programs, ${terms.technology.agentSwarm}, Declare ${terms.systems.agi}, and ${terms.technology.advancedGeneration}. Earlier unused ${terms.systems.escalations} remain available.

playerReferences.name: A Perfectly Governed Quarter
frontText: 1. Begin the Era: ready Core Actions, draw Headlines, and reveal the ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
2. Three cycles: reveal ${terms.systems.headline}, SELECT, reveal, MOVE, ACT, exhaust.
3. Resolve ${terms.infrastructure.power} and Production.
4. Conduct the ${terms.systems.publicAudit}.
5. Score the ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.
6. Default Game: advance directly after Era III Mandate scoring. Advanced Play only: secretly ballot, reveal, and resolve ${terms.systems.realignment}.
backText: SELECT one unused Core Action or one legal unused ${terms.systems.escalation}.
MOVE one acting piece 0–2 hexes, then ACT from its destination.
Apply at most one destination bonus, one Faction modifier, one Tactic, and the ${terms.systems.headline}.
Only ${terms.technology.agentSwarm} resolves additional Core Actions.
${terms.systems.escalations} spend 1 Escalation availability. Unspent availability expires.
If an effect says lowest, highest, or most and ties, use Initiative-clockwise order.
playerReferences.flavorText: Every quarter is unprecedented. The sequence remains standardized.

playerReferences.name: Infrastructure and Accountability
frontText: Default Game: the starting grid powers its assigned Facility; each Generator powers only its own or adjacent Facilities.
Assign local ${terms.infrastructure.power}, then produce powered Facilities. Advanced Play instead recalculates and pools the connected Network.
After allocation, mark every fully powered Facility Grid-Ready; remove its marker if it moves, disconnects, or later receives insufficient ${terms.infrastructure.power}.
Gain ${terms.playerTracks.customer} income and Joint Venture production. Advanced Play also grants the Network bonus.
Offline Facilities retain presence but do not produce.
backText: Audit draws = round(base draws × players ÷ 4), minimum 1.
For each cube drawn, its owner pays 1 ${terms.resources.runway} or loses 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
A Systemic Risk cube affects every player with at least 3 ${terms.playerTracks.customers}.
If your ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} supply is empty, each additional cube costs 1 ${terms.resources.runway} or 1 ${terms.playerTracks.trust} immediately.
playerReferences.flavorText: Capacity is local by default. Responsibility remains individually addressable.

playerReferences.name: Advanced Play: The Map Has Approved a Motion
frontText: Every player secretly chooses one ballot; reveal simultaneously.
Plurality wins. For tied leading motions, scan ballots from Initiative clockwise.
Core: inner ring +1 clockwise.
Periphery: outer ring +1 clockwise.
Counter-Cycle: inner +1 clockwise; outer −1.
backText: ${terms.locations.frontier} never moves; moving tiles carry all site-bound contents.
Recalculate Network reach; never lift or re-lay edge segments.
Disconnected contracts remain owned but produce nothing.
An edge-split ${terms.technology.megaCluster} is offline until its Facilities are adjacent.
Use only in Advanced Play, exactly once after Era III Mandate scoring; skip in every other Era.
playerReferences.flavorText: The geography remains factual. Its location has been updated.

playerReferences.name: History Is a Public Track
frontText: ${terms.playerTracks.customers} 1–3 score 2 ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} each; ${terms.playerTracks.customers} 4–5 score 1 each. Every ${terms.playerTracks.customer} still produces 1 ${terms.resources.runway}.
Immediately score 2 once at ${terms.playerTracks.capability} 3, 6, 9, and 12, except for a printed faction scoring rule.
Immediately score 2 once at ${terms.playerTracks.trust} 2, 4, and 6.
Printed Era, ${terms.systems.headline}, Faction, Fusion, and ${terms.systems.agi} awards score immediately.
backText: Threshold ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} never reverses if a track later falls.
Facilities and control do not automatically score.
Baseline game: Tactics and secret objectives are not used.
Final scoring: −1 per offline Facility.
AGI emerges when a declaration finishes at Capability 9+. Open requires final Collective Trust at least setup total + player count and unresolved Systemic Risk below player count.
Emerges/Open: The Singularity; Emerges/Closed: The Closed Loop; no AGI/Open: The Plural Future; no AGI/Closed: Assured Continuity.
playerReferences.flavorText: Mandate is public permission to shape the future: credibility during ${terms.eras.demo}, capacity during ${terms.eras.scale}, authority during ${terms.eras.narrative}, and historical legitimacy during ${terms.eras.claim}.

objectives.name: Quietly Indispensable
objectives.rulesText: At game end, have at least 2 powered Facilities and no more than 4 ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} cubes in the bag.
objectives.flavorText: Nobody knows what the institution does. Every institution depends on it.

objectives.name: Too Big to Pause
objectives.rulesText: At game end, have at least 3 ${terms.playerTracks.customers} and ${terms.playerTracks.trust} of 3 or less.
objectives.flavorText: Public confidence is temporary. Integration contracts are forever.

objectives.name: Benevolent Monopoly
objectives.rulesText: At game end, have at least 3 ${terms.playerTracks.customers} and at least 4 ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
objectives.flavorText: Everyone selected the default because the default selected everyone.

objectives.name: Institutional Capture
objectives.rulesText: At game end, control at least 2 of Media, Government, and Capital.

endings.name: The Singularity
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} emerges and the ending is Open.
endings.text: The system has crossed the relevant threshold, and nobody can reduce it to a product category without being contradicted in public. Its authority remains contested: institutions publish objections, communities make demands, and the new intelligence must answer both. Transformation arrives unevenly, with no guarantee of comfort, but living people retain standing to redirect its use.

endings.name: The Closed Loop
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} emerges and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: Capability has crossed the threshold inside an institution already optimized to prevent meaningful reply. Growth engines, debt clocks, power contracts, and quarterly objectives become an airtight execution loop. The operators eventually disappear; the infrastructure continues, treating every remaining objection as a ticket that has successfully entered the queue.

endings.name: The Plural Future
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} does not emerge and the ending is Open.
endings.text: No declaration survives the printed test, yet the world does not collapse into a single successor. Useful systems remain bounded, distributed, and subject to revision. Progress is slower than the announcements promised and more durable than the headlines expected. Many institutions retain the standing to argue about what should be built next, which is inconvenient and therefore alive.

endings.name: Assured Continuity
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} does not emerge and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: No system becomes genuinely general. The distinction stops mattering to the institutions that have already automated their obligations into permanence. Maintenance authorities renew one another, models classify appeals into acceptable delay, and every public concern receives a service-level response. The future remains technically human, provided nobody asks who can still change it.

box.frontStrapline: ${terms.actions.build} the future. ${terms.infrastructure.power} the future. Announce the future before anyone else.
box.backCopy: The prototype worked. That was sufficient. Across a modular jurisdiction of thirteen contested districts, six institutions now compete for the capacity to make its consequences unavoidable: compute, talent, energy, customers, and permission to call dependency progress. Choose only three priorities each quarter. ${terms.actions.build} powered networks. Push Training Runs until they succeed or collapse. Negotiate infrastructure with rivals who will later call the arrangement responsible. Manage public ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} while increasingly indefensible options become available. In the final Era, deploy agent swarms, ignite a fusion demonstrator, and report that ${terms.systems.agi} has been achieved.
box.shortPitch: A strategy game about six institutions racing across a modular jurisdiction to make ${terms.systems.agi} necessary before anyone agrees what it is.
box.contentWarning: Satirical themes include layoffs, surveillance-adjacent institutions, energy consumption, political influence, and technological crisis.

worldPrimer: The new intelligence arrived first as software: near-instant code, cheap expertise, limitless media, and systems that solved problems across mathematics, science, engineering, and medicine once thought beyond automation. Then it became the default layer through which society operated. Work, research, public services, and everyday life reorganized around models that no institution fully understood or controlled.

The institutions building those models became physical powers. Intelligence required land, water, chips, electricity, capital, secure networks, and permission to keep expanding. Governments continued approving the projects because essential services, economic growth, and national security increasingly depended on them.

Six institutions now compete to define what comes next. They begin by selling intelligence. They end by competing for infrastructure, public legitimacy, and the right to declare that they have achieved artificial general intelligence. No one agrees what that means. Several institutions have already claimed they did.

# ${content.worldCopy.title}
## A strategy game about institutions turning reliable AI capability into contested public authority as they build, deploy, regulate, and race to declare ${terms.systems.agi}

**Suggested player count:** ${game.suggestedPlayerRange}

## Play profiles

**Default Game** is authoritative in this book, the browser, and simulation.
Use the browser **First Game Guide** for an accelerated Default Game.
[**Advanced Play**](/docs/advanced-play.html) is an extension layer with additional complexity.
**Advanced Play** is selected before setup and must be used for the entire game or not used at all.

The symbol **◆** marks a rule that changes in Advanced Play.
Use the base rule in Default Game, then apply the corresponding change from
the [**Advanced Play supplement**](/docs/advanced-play.html).

The separately printed [**World and Institutions**](/docs/world-and-institutions.html) companion contains setting
and ending narratives.

## How to Play

Default Game lasts four Eras. The institution with the most ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} wins; resolve that winner and the shared World Ending separately. Follow the numbered sections in order.

## 1. Setup

1. ${terms.actions.build} the thirteen-tile board as described in **Modular hex board**:
   ${terms.locations.frontier} in the center, the shuffled six-tile operational ring around it,
   and the shuffled six-tile public ring in the evenly spaced outer positions.
2. Separate the ${terms.systems.headline} cards by Era. **◆** Use only the
   Default-eligible cards: cards without an **Advanced Play** badge. Shuffle
   each eligible Era deck and place it beside its Era card. Each Era uses three
   ${terms.systems.headlines}.
   Leave room below the four Era cards for the twelve-card ${terms.systems.futureTimeline}.
3. Shuffle the Training deck. Separate the twelve Era ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} cards into
   four three-card Era decks. Shuffle each deck and place it beside the
   matching Era card.
4. Place ${terms.resources.runway}, ${terms.resources.compute}, ${terms.resources.safety}, ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}, Systemic Risk,
   Joint Venture, ${terms.technology.megaCluster}, Initiative, and Audit bag
   components within reach. Place the ${terms.infrastructure.power} Source reference cards nearby.
5. Each player chooses or receives one Faction. Take its board, six Core
   Actions, seven ${terms.systems.escalations}, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided
   Facilities, one Generator, one ${terms.playerTracks.customer}-track marker, one
   Escalation-track marker, one reversible Declare ${terms.systems.agi} card,
   remaining track markers, and starting resources.
6. Place every CEO and one Team at ${terms.locations.frontier}. Keep the other two Teams in
   supply. Set each Faction’s ${terms.resources.runway}, ${terms.resources.compute}, ${terms.playerTracks.capability}, ${terms.playerTracks.customers}, ${terms.playerTracks.trust},
   and ${terms.resources.safety} to its printed starting values.
7. Place each Faction’s already-earned public ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} on the shared track as
   printed on its Faction board. Put every player’s ten ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny}
   cubes outside the bag; the bag begins empty.
8. Add every Faction’s printed starting ${terms.playerTracks.trust} and record the result as
   **Setup Collective ${terms.playerTracks.trust}** on the Era reference. This fixed value is used
   during the World Ending.
9. Choose Initiative randomly and give that player the Initiative marker.
   Begin Era I.

Do not deal Tactics or secret objectives in the baseline game.

## 2. Central loop

Each player has six Core Action cards but takes only three turns per Era.
Once played, a Core Action remains exhausted until the next Era:

- ${terms.actions.fund}
- ${terms.actions.research}
- ${terms.actions.build}
- ${terms.actions.organize}
- ${terms.actions.deploy}
- ${terms.actions.influence}

Choose three of six Actions each Era, in any order. The other three remain
unused unless an ability readies one.

### The complete ordinary turn: Select → Move → Act

1. Reveal one ${terms.systems.headline}.
2. Every player secretly selects one unused Core Action, or spends one
   Escalation availability to select one unlocked Escalation.
3. Reveal every selected action simultaneously.
4. Resolve clockwise from Initiative.
5. **Select:** the revealed Action is the only Action this turn.
6. **Move:** choose one acting piece and move it zero, one, or two adjacent
   hexes.
7. **Act:** read the chosen Action card from top to bottom and resolve it from
   the destination.
8. Exhaust the Core Action, or spend one Escalation availability and flip the Escalation.
9. Pass Initiative clockwise before the next cycle.

Selection commits the Action card; choose the piece, path, target, and payment
during resolution.

### Acting piece

The acting piece is a CEO or Team. Both can take any Action; a CEO contributes
two presence and a Team one. Its destination determines where Facilities and
power infrastructure may be built, where Research and Deploy occur, which
location bonus applies, and which political spaces may be Influenced.

Facilities and Generators cannot act. ${terms.actions.organize}
receives normal acting-piece movement before its additional movement,
recruitment, restructuring, or relocation.

### Effect precedence ◆

Apply these sources in order:

- The Era card determines globally unlocked actions.
- A Faction board modifies those actions.
- The current ${terms.systems.headline} supplies its printed global effect.
- An ordinary turn may apply the Action, one destination bonus, one Faction
  modifier, and each applicable global effect.
- Every exception is timed **before selection**, **during movement**, **during
  action**, or **after action**.
- A ${terms.systems.headline} changes one named field or calls one public choice procedure. It
  grants no additional Action.
- Readying a card makes it available for a later choice. Resolve nothing when
  you ready it.
- ${terms.technology.agentSwarm} is the sole compound-action exception.

### What an Era teaches

Systems are inactive before their Era card lists them under **New this Era**.
Read that strip aloud before revealing the Mandate. All Era cards,
Escalations, and Faction abilities are open information.

Escalation is cumulative. Progress teaches ordinary institutional work;
Capacity adds industrial infrastructure; Authority adds agreements, quantum
record disputes, and public effects; Continuity adds compound Actions, declarations, and exceptional
generation. Later Eras retain previously unlocked systems
unless a printed effect says otherwise.

### Universal tie rule

Whenever an effect targets the player with the lowest, highest, or most of
something and multiple players tie, target the tied player nearest Initiative
clockwise. An effect that explicitly applies to everyone, or explicitly awards
all tied players, overrides this rule.

Initiative is an order, not a resource. Passing it after each cycle changes who
resolves first and who wins unresolved ties; it cannot be traded or retained.

### Escalation availability and ${terms.systems.escalations}

Gain, spend, and lose **Escalation availability** on your faction-board track.
Spend one availability to select an Era-unlocked Escalation:

- Select an ${terms.systems.escalation} instead of a Core Action.
- Commit and reduce the Escalation availability track by one.
- Flip the ${terms.systems.escalation} after resolution.
- Each named ${terms.systems.escalation} is usable once per player per game.
- Unspent Escalation availability expires at Era end.
- Previously unlocked unused ${terms.systems.escalations} remain available later.

**Global after movement** means the acting piece moves normally, then the
Action resolves without a destination restriction.

| Era | Availability gained | Newly available ${terms.systems.escalations} |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| I — ${terms.eras.demo} | 0 | None |
| II — ${terms.eras.scale} | 1 | ${terms.technology.megaCluster}, Reorganization |
| III — ${terms.eras.narrative} | 1 | Open Weights, Narrative Capture |
| IV — ${terms.eras.claim} | 2 | ${terms.technology.agentSwarm}, Declare ${terms.systems.agi}, ${terms.technology.advancedGeneration} |

${terms.technology.agentSwarm} is the selected Escalation; it resolves and exhausts two
different unused Core Actions.

### A committed Action that becomes blocked

After reveal, choose any legal piece, movement, mode, target, payment, and
immediate trade, but never replace the selected Action.

If an earlier player consumes every legal Facility space, Generator slot,
contract token, or other required target, movement still resolves and the
Action exhausts without effect or compensation. Initiative can therefore let
an earlier player consume a later player’s target. Do not rewind simultaneous
selection.

## 3. Resources

### ${terms.resources.runway}, ${terms.resources.compute}, and ${terms.playerTracks.capability}

- **${terms.resources.runway}:** financing spent on Facilities, hiring, partnerships,
  lobbying, and crises.
- **${terms.resources.compute}:** capacity spent on ${terms.actions.research}, ${terms.actions.deploy}, and infrastructure.
- **${terms.playerTracks.capability}:** permanent model quality that unlocks Deployments and
  ${terms.systems.agi}; spend it only when instructed.

### ${terms.playerTracks.customers}

Each ${terms.playerTracks.customer} produces one ${terms.resources.runway} during Production. Customers #1–3 immediately score two public ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}; Customers #4–5 score one each. Customers also increase public exposure.

### ${terms.playerTracks.trust}

A zero-to-six track affecting regulation, Joint Ventures, safety, and the
final declaration. Zero ${terms.playerTracks.trust} does not eliminate a player.

**${terms.playerTracks.mandate}** is the score used to determine the winner (victory points).
It is the public authority you have gained to define outcomes.
It represents the recognized right to shape the future: credibility in Progress,
capacity in Capacity, authority in Authority, and historical legitimacy in
Continuity.

${terms.playerTracks.mandate} is normally scored immediately on one public track:

- Two when ${terms.playerTracks.customer} #1, #2, or #3 is gained; one when #4 or #5 is gained.
- Two the first time ${terms.playerTracks.capability} reaches three, six, nine, and twelve, except
  for a printed faction scoring rule.
- Two the first time ${terms.playerTracks.trust} reaches two, four, and six.
- Printed ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} from ${terms.systems.headlines}, Era Mandates, Fusion, faction abilities,
  and ${terms.systems.agi}.

Threshold awards are permanent; later losses do not reverse them.

There is no hidden or deferred conversion of Facilities, controlled hexes,
stored resources, or unused cards into ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}. If an effect scores ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}, move
the public marker when that effect resolves.

### Universal costs and caps

Apply resource caps immediately after any gain or trade:

- ${terms.resources.runway}: twelve
- ${terms.resources.compute}: ten
- ${terms.resources.safety}: three, except a printed Faction limit

Return excess. A trade cannot move resources through a player above a cap.

When effects change a cost, apply replacements and waivers first, then
surcharges, then discounts. The final cost cannot fall below zero.

## 4. Modular hex board

The board is one jurisdiction whose districts represent physical and
institutional dependencies rather than ordinary distance. The [**Map reference**](/map-reference.html)
is authoritative for its thirteen-tile setup, adjacency, ring pools, tile
effects, Facility spaces, presence, and control. The shuffled map remains
fixed for all four Eras. **◆**

One movement step crosses one shared tile edge; an acting CEO or Team may move
zero, one, or two steps. Every piece placed during setup begins at
${terms.locations.frontier}. Rival pieces coexist; there is no combat or player
elimination.

### ${terms.infrastructure.power} connections ◆

Default Game uses **local Power**, not a Network graph. The starting grid
powers only its assigned first Facility. Each Generator powers only Facilities
on its own hex or an adjacent hex. A Facility cannot pass Power onward to
another Facility.

Recalculate local eligibility whenever a Facility or Generator moves; do not
preserve a connection the visible board no longer supports.

### Contract hosts

Joint Ventures and Mega-Clusters use shared, matched token pairs. Create one
only while its pair is available; place one numbered half on each host.

A contract remains owned but is active only while its fixed hosts meet its
requirements. Tokens travel with their Facilities.

Every cross-player contract or jointly funded project requires the explicit
consent of every participant. Facilities sharing one hex are **co-located**.
Adjacent host Facilities occupy hexes that share an edge.

Consent applies to the named project only. It does not grant control of a host,
create a general trading right, or authorize another contract. A contract’s
matched number preserves its identity when a host moves.

### Joint Venture

${terms.actions.influence} may create a Joint Venture between two adjacent Facilities owned by
different players, unless a Faction ability explicitly changes that range.
Both host Facilities must be powered during Production for the contract to
produce.

Each partner gains the resource shown by the **contract icon on the other
host tile**. Do not copy full tile production or multiply it with Facility
effects.

During ${terms.actions.influence}, make one complete proposal naming both eligible hosts and
the partner. Acceptance creates it. Rejection, pass, or no response uses that
effect; do not choose another partner or ${terms.actions.influence} effect.

Either participant may instead use ${terms.actions.influence} to terminate one shared Joint
Venture. Return its pair. Termination cannot be combined with another
${terms.actions.influence} effect.

### ${terms.infrastructure.power} delivery ◆

${terms.infrastructure.power} is Production capacity and cannot be stored.

- Every player begins with a basic one-${terms.infrastructure.power} grid connection. It automatically
  powers that player’s first Facility, requires no recurring payment,
  and cannot supply the additional demand of ${terms.technology.megaCluster}. It is
  dedicated capacity and cannot be sold. Place the
  player’s starting-grid state on that first Facility.
- Every Facility needs one delivered ${terms.infrastructure.power} to produce.
- A ${terms.technology.megaCluster} needs two additional ${terms.infrastructure.power}.
- The starting-grid state and each Generator’s own or
  adjacent Facilities are the only legal recipients. A Generator does not need
  to be connected to the starting-grid Facility.

Power never travels through an opponent’s sites unless a specific purchase
rule transfers that capacity. A sale changes available capacity, not the map.

Follow **${terms.infrastructure.power} and Production**. Capacity powers Facilities and projects,
produces no resources, and may be assigned only once. Assign each local source
only among its legal recipients.

An offline Facility still occupies space, contributes presence, and may be
visited, but produces nothing. Sufficient Power in a later Production returns
it online.

- Only Core Actions
