## 6. Era sequence

### A. Begin the quarter

- Advance to the next fixed Era card.
- Read that Era’s **New this Era** strip aloud. Those systems are now active.
- Reveal one ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} from the current Era’s three-card deck. Return the other
  two cards in that deck to the box unseen.
- Ready all six Core Actions.
- Award Escalation availability.

### B. Three action cycles

At the beginning of each cycle:

1. Reveal a ${terms.systems.headline} and place it in the current Era’s ${terms.systems.futureTimeline} row.
2. Everyone secretly **selects** one Action card.
3. Reveal simultaneously.
4. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: **move**, then **act**.
5. Pass Initiative clockwise.

#### Immediate resource trade ◆

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete
resource offer to one rival, naming each type and amount. That rival accepts
or rejects, or publishes one complete counteroffer. The original offer-maker
accepts or rejects that counteroffer. Rejection, pass, or no response ends the
window; do not redirect or renegotiate. A counteroffer cannot receive another
counteroffer.
${terms.resources.runway}, ${terms.resources.compute}, and ${terms.resources.safety} tokens may be exchanged. Every accepted component changes hands
immediately; promises about later turns are not binding. The active
${terms.systems.headline} may prohibit a named resource from being traded.

Without acceptance, continue the selected Action; resolve it as blocked if no
legal resolution remains.

Immediate resource trades require no ${terms.actions.influence} Action. Only ${terms.actions.influence} creates
persistent Joint Ventures, lobbying effects, or ${terms.playerTracks.trust} manipulation.

### Negotiation and paced play

Discussion creates no game state, obligation, or Action. Promises about later
turns remain non-binding. Apply formal choices only in their printed windows;
missing responses are rejection or pass.

**Paced Play** is an optional table rule. Before play, the group may assign one
shared sand timer to each negotiation window. When it expires, discussion ends
and the normal rejection or pass fallback applies. Expiry never
creates consent or forces a deal.

### C. ${terms.infrastructure.power} and Production

Every player board presents the same five Production boxes. Resolve a box for
every player before advancing to the next box:

1. **Generate:** determine every Generator’s local eligible Facilities. Every
   Generator with at least one eligible Facility operates automatically. Add one ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} for every
   ${terms.technology.emergencyInfrastructure}. Add any ${terms.systems.headline} generation.
2. **Trade ◆:** in Initiative order, each player may make one ${terms.infrastructure.power}
   purchase request to one adjacent rival Power connection. The named supplier accepts
   or rejects. A rejected, passed, or unanswered request fails; the buyer then
   allocates with the ${terms.infrastructure.power} they have. An accepted buyer pays one
   ${terms.resources.runway} per ${terms.infrastructure.power} directly to the consenting supplier. Each supplier may sell
   at most one ${terms.infrastructure.power} this Production. Only installed Generator or Fusion
   capacity may be sold; starting-grid and emergency ${terms.infrastructure.power} may not.
3. **Allocate:** add starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency ${terms.infrastructure.power};
   allocate it only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters.
   Flip every Facility receiving its complete demand to Grid-Ready; flip every
   Facility that does not back to its normal face.
4. **Produce:** produce powered Facilities, one ${terms.resources.runway} per ${terms.playerTracks.customer},
   and active Mega-Clusters, in that order.
5. **Partner:** produce active Joint Ventures in ascending contract-number
   order.

Complete each box for every player before entering the next. Do not let one
player finish Production while others still generate, trade, or allocate. This
keeps sales and contracts tied to one visible capacity state. Within a box,
resolve in Initiative order unless that box specifies otherwise.

Purchased ${terms.infrastructure.power} lasts only this Production and creates no contract or
future obligation. A supplier may leave its own Facility offline.

Apply the universal resource caps after every Production gain.

### D. ${terms.systems.publicAudit}

Risky actions add player-colored ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} to the opaque Audit bag. Each
player has ten cubes. For each required cube when all ten are already in the
bag, immediately pay one ${terms.resources.runway} or lose one ${terms.playerTracks.trust}; take the available option if
only one exists. If neither exists, suffer no further loss. A depleted supply
never makes a risky action free.

The four-player base draws are two, three, four, and five. For other player
counts, calculate each Era’s draw count as:

> round(base draws × player count ÷ 4), minimum one

Era halves upward. The resulting Audit profiles are:

| Era | 2 players | 3 players | 4 players | 5 players | 6 players |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| I | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| II | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| III | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| IV | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 |

Draw the listed number of cubes or stop when the bag is empty.

In Eras I–III, each colored cube makes its owner pay one ${terms.resources.runway} or lose one
${terms.playerTracks.trust}. Take the available option if only one exists; if neither exists, suffer
no further loss.

In Era IV, each colored cube makes its owner pay two ${terms.resources.runway} or lose one
${terms.playerTracks.mandate}. The payment is indivisible. With fewer than two ${terms.resources.runway}, lose one
${terms.playerTracks.mandate} if possible; at zero ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}, reduce ${terms.resources.runway} to zero. ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} cannot fall
below zero.

Drawn player-colored cubes return to the owner’s supply; undrawn cubes remain
in the bag.

${terms.locations.media} Facilities may remove cubes before the draw. A drawn black Systemic
Risk cube gives every player with at least three ${terms.playerTracks.customers} the current Era’s
penalty, then returns to supply. Apply the same availability rules. Black cubes
remaining at game end are unresolved Systemic Risk.

### E. Score the ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}

Each Era ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} has a minimum qualification. If nobody qualifies, nobody
scores it. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores two ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}; tied qualifying
leaders score one ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} each.

Compare only the revealed Mandate’s printed criterion. Resources, control, and
public score do not break its tie. Leave the scored card beside its Era as part
of the table’s public history.

The revealed Mandate card is the exact qualification and scoring authority.

- Location: ${terms.locations.grid}
- Cost: one ${terms.resources.runway}
- Capacity: four ${terms.infrastructure.power}
- Add one ${terms.playerTracks.scrutiny} during every Production

### ${terms.technology.advancedGeneration}

The Era IV ${terms.systems.escalation} described above.

## 9. Printed card authorities

Faction boards, Core Action cards, Escalation cards, Era cards, Mandate cards,
Training cards, Power cards, and Headline cards are rules components. The
[**Card reference**](/card-reference.html) projects every card face in one document; resolve that text
or the matching physical card. Card text changes only the field or timing it
names; it does not create an unprinted phase or additional Action.

All Factions and CEOs are fictional and imply no real-world claim or
endorsement. Every Faction has one persistent institutional identity and one
signature program. Timing is **passive**, **once per Era**, **once when
unlocked**, or **once per game**. “Persists” remains available; “named Era
only” expires at Era end. Faction abilities modify named timing windows; they
add no phase.

During setup, use each Faction board’s printed starts and place its already
earned public ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}. Award that ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} once; never score it
again. The Faction board is authoritative if a summary elsewhere differs.

A Headline is revealed before secret action selection. Resolve its printed
effect and duration. Leave it face up in its Era row. Three Headlines per Era
form the twelve-card **${terms.systems.futureTimeline}**. A Headline grants no Action. Unless
its text names this Era’s Production, its rules expire at the end of the
current cycle.

## 10. Map and component reference

Use [**Map reference**](/map-reference.html) for setup, adjacency, location effects, presence, and
control. Use [**Component reference**](/component-reference.html) for deck contracts, component limits, and
defined markers. Use [**Card reference**](/card-reference.html) for every card face. Those references
are part of the Default Game, not optional background.
## 11. Final scoring

All earned ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} is already on the public track. Do not score it again.

At game end:

1. Read the twelve ${terms.systems.headlines} in the ${terms.systems.futureTimeline} aloud, Era by Era.
2. Lose one ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} for each offline Facility.
3. Resolve the shared World Ending.
4. Announce the highest-${terms.playerTracks.mandate} institution only after reading the history it
   claims to have won.

Offline penalties cannot reduce a player below zero ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.

There is no other endgame scoring.

### The shared World Ending

Determine one institutional winner and one shared ending from visible state:

- Count the ${terms.systems.agi} declarations.
- Total every player’s final ${terms.playerTracks.trust}.
- Count unresolved Systemic Risk cubes remaining in the Audit bag.

First determine whether ${terms.systems.agi} emerges. It emerges if:

- At least one declaring institution finishes the game at ${terms.playerTracks.capability} nine or
  higher.

Then determine whether the ending is **Open**. It is Open only if both
conditions are true:

- Final Collective ${terms.playerTracks.trust} is at least Setup Collective ${terms.playerTracks.trust} plus the player
  count.
- Unresolved Systemic Risk is lower than the player count.

Collective ${terms.playerTracks.trust} is every player’s total; individuals need not exceed their
own starting value.

If either Open condition fails, the ending is **Closed**. A qualified ${terms.systems.agi}
declaration does not by itself make the ending Open.

Cross the two results to find the shared World Ending:

| | Open | Closed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ${terms.systems.agi} emerges | **The Singularity** | **The Closed Loop** |
| ${terms.systems.agi} does not emerge | **The Plural Future** | **Assured Continuity** |

Read its narrative from [**World and Institutions**](/docs/world-and-institutions.html). Facilities and control
score no separate endgame ${terms.playerTracks.mandate}.

Keep the draft secret objectives out of the baseline game, balance evidence,
and duration evidence.

Highest ${terms.playerTracks.mandate} wins.

Ties break by:

1. Higher ${terms.playerTracks.trust}
2. More ${terms.playerTracks.customers}
3. More ${terms.resources.compute}
4. Joint victory accompanied by an extremely serious merger announcement

Find design rationale and balance qualification in
[**Balance and Exploitability**](/docs/balance-and-exploitability.html). Find observation
protocols in [**Playtesting and Evidence**](/docs/playtesting-and-evidence.html).

## Advanced Play

The separate [**Advanced Play supplement**](/docs/advanced-play.html) is the complete authority for the
bundled Advanced profile. Do not import one Advanced procedure into Default
Game.

# ${content.worldCopy.title} — Advanced Play Supplement

Advanced Play is one bundled profile. Apply every change below; do not select
individual modules. All unlisted rules remain exactly as written for Default
Game. The **◆** symbol in the Default Rules identifies a rule this supplement
extends or replaces.

${content.ruleChangeRegister.profileComparison}

## Setup

Each player takes two Link tokens, one Network marker and capacity track, and
three ${terms.systems.realignment} ballots in addition to their Default Game components. Add the
six-sided Volatility die to the shared supply. Build each Headline deck from
every card for its Era, including cards with an **Advanced Play** badge.

## Connected infrastructure

Advanced Play replaces local Power with a connected ${terms.systems.infrastructureNetwork}.
The same graph governs ${terms.infrastructure.power} delivery and the Network production bonus:

- The first Facility joins through the basic grid connection.
- Owned Facilities and Generators on the same or adjacent hexes connect to one
  another.
- A Link on one otherwise disconnected Facility joins that Facility to the
  Network. Owned sites adjacent to it may then connect normally.
- ${terms.infrastructure.power} from connected Generators and purchased ${terms.infrastructure.power} is pooled across the
  Network.
- Beginning in Era II, two or more connected, powered Facilities produce one
  additional ${terms.resources.runway} or ${terms.resources.compute}.

Award at most one Network bonus per player. Use this graph for Power delivery
and production; do not calculate edge-by-edge flow. Recalculate the whole
Network when a Facility or Link moves or changes.

Beginning in Era II, **Infrastructure Build** may Install a Link: pay one
${terms.resources.runway} and place one of your Link tokens on the Facility at the acting piece’s
destination. That Facility joins your Network even if otherwise disconnected;
owned sites adjacent to it may then connect normally. A Facility holds at most
one Link and carries it when moved.

A solo Mega-Cluster requires both hosts in its owner’s Network. A joint
Mega-Cluster requires each host in its owner’s Network. When a Facility moves,
recalculate its owner’s Network and every affected contract. Flip a Facility
back to its normal face when it leaves its owner’s Network.

## Immediate resource trades

After the named rival publishes a counteroffer, every eligible player other
than the counteroffer maker—including the original offer maker—may
simultaneously pass or claim it instead of giving the original maker the sole
accept-or-reject decision. The counteroffer maker chooses one claimant or
declines them all. A chosen claim completes immediately, even if neither party
is the active player.

There are no further offers or counteroffers in that resolution. A
counteroffer with no claimant, or with all claimants declined, expires. The
active player then continues the selected Action under the normal blocked-Action
rule if necessary.

## Production ${terms.infrastructure.power} requests

In Advanced Play, each player may make up to two Production Power purchase
requests, each to a different adjacent rival Network. A rejection does not
consume the second request. Supplier limits, price, eligible capacity, and all
other Production rules remain unchanged.

## Headline procedures

Every Headline card is eligible. Resolve exactly one printed badge procedure
per card:

- **DIRECTIVE:** resolve an instruction or modify one field for its duration.
- **SECRET CHOICE:** everyone chooses simultaneously, then reveals.
- **CIVIC PERMISSION AUTHORITY VOTE:** everyone secretly votes and reveals
  together. The ${terms.locations.government} controller’s vote counts twice and breaks a tie;
  Initiative breaks it if ${terms.locations.government} is uncontrolled.
- **AUCTION:** everyone secretly bids from zero to their current
  ${terms.resources.runway}, then reveals. The highest positive bidder pays and wins. Ties use
  Initiative-clockwise order; all-zero bidding has no winner.
- **VOLATILITY:** roll only when instructed. A two-result roll uses 1–3 for the
  first result and 4–6 for the second unless the card states otherwise.

An immediate instruction resolves before action selection. Unless stated
otherwise, an effect lasts for the current cycle; an effect naming this Era’s
Production remains until Production, and a remainder-of-game result becomes
shared public state. Place a persistent Headline beside the affected Action as
a reminder. The current Headline overrides an older persistent Headline on the
same field; effects on other fields remain active. There is no separate Law
system or Law deck.

## Era III ${terms.systems.realignment}

Resolve ${terms.systems.realignment} exactly once, after Era III Mandate scoring. Skip it in
every other Era. Each player secretly chooses and simultaneously reveals one
ballot:

- **Consolidate the Core:** rotate the six inner-ring locations one position
  clockwise.
- **Expand the Periphery:** rotate the six outer-ring locations one position
  clockwise.
- **Authorize Counter-Cycle:** rotate the inner ring one position clockwise
  and the outer ring one position counterclockwise.

A player who places no ballot names no motion and cannot break a tie. The motion
with the most ballots wins. If leading motions tie, scan clockwise from
Initiative; the first player whose ballot names a tied motion chooses it. If
none does, Initiative chooses. Government bonuses and other vote modifiers do
not apply.

${terms.locations.frontier} never moves. Each moving tile carries every CEO, Team, Facility,
Generator and other site-bound component. Rotate the
selected physical ring once, then recalculate every Network from its
starting-grid Facility, Links, and visible adjacency. Do not lift or re-lay
components.

A ring rotation carries each Facility and its Grid-Ready face together.
After recalculating each ${terms.systems.infrastructureNetwork}, flip back any
Facility now outside its owner’s Network.

Joint Ventures remain owned but operate only while their fixed hosts are
adjacent and meet all requirements. Mega-Clusters whose hosts are no longer
adjacent are offline until adjacency returns. Matched tokens travel with their
host Facilities. Immediate ${terms.infrastructure.power} purchases do not persist through Realignment.
Realignment destroys no component, changes no host, and terminates no contract.

Ballot options are public; choices remain secret until simultaneous reveal.
Players may discuss and signal, but those statements are non-binding. The
procedure above alone chooses the motion. Every player then has Era IV’s three
Actions to respond to the changed geography.

motions.flavorText: The edge has been moved closer to opportunity without changing its distance.

motions.name: Authorize Counter-Cycle
motions.ballotText: Rotate the inner ring one position clockwise and the outer ring one position counterclockwise.
motions.flavorText: Competing jurisdictions have synchronized by moving in opposite directions.

realignment.name: Advanced Play: Jurisdictional Realignment
realignment.timing: Advanced Play only: exactly once, after Mandate scoring in Era III.
realignment.vote: Every player secretly selects one motion. Reveal simultaneously. The motion with the most ballots resolves.
realignment.tieBreak: Among tied leading motions, scan players clockwise from Initiative; the first ballot naming a tied motion selects it.
realignment.contentsRule: Location tiles and everything on them move together. Frontier never moves.
realignment.networkRule: After movement, recalculate Network reach from the starting-grid Facility, Generators, Link-marked Facilities, and visible adjacency. No pieces are lifted or re-laid.
realignment.agreementRule: Joint Ventures and Mega-Clusters remain owned but produce only while their required Facilities are adjacent. Immediate Power purchases never persist through Realignment.

startingGridConnection.restrictions: Cannot supply Mega-Cluster demand and cannot be sold.

tiles.name: Frontier
tiles.visit: After Act, you may gain 1 Runway and add 1 Scrutiny.
tiles.flavorText: The jurisdiction’s standing civic exception: new systems are authorized as temporary, beneficial, and voluntary before society must organize around them.

tiles.name: Research Commons
tiles.flavorText: Publicly chartered inquiry remains nominally shared while institutions compete to privatize its results, standards, and future uses.

tiles.name: Compute Estate
tiles.visit: Reduce the first Compute cost by 1.
tiles.flavorText: Cooling plant, water compact, and model contract now arrive as one planning application.

tiles.name: Human Access District
tiles.flavorText: Every resident may opt out through the account settings of the service they require.

tiles.name: Fabrication Corridor
tiles.flavorText: Yield, water, labor, and export priority are negotiated at the same loading gate.

tiles.name: Allocation Exchange
tiles.flavorText: Future capacity is priced before the people who will depend on it are asked.

tiles.name: Workforce Transition District
tiles.flavorText: Every transition program includes an exit path for the work it was created to preserve.

tiles.name: Consensus Network
tiles.flavorText: A public is assembled from attention, verification, and the version of events that arrives on time.

tiles.name: Civic Permission Authority
tiles.flavorText: A temporary authorization remains voluntary until every essential service requires it.

tiles.name: Power Corridor
tiles.visit: Build Emergency Power Complex here for 1 Runway.
tiles.flavorText: Every promised future submits one more request for transmission, cooling, and priority.

tiles.name: Thermal and Water Basin
tiles.visit: Build Civic Heat Battery here for 2 Runway.
tiles.flavorText: Clean power, water, and thermal relief become one indivisible public ledger.

cards.name: Code
cards.flavorText: Operational records, software practice, and every abstraction that survived deployment.

cards.name: Science
cards.flavorText: Replicated findings, disputed methods, and research that can still be made legible.

cards.name: The Web
cards.flavorText: A public archive of knowledge, commerce, argument, and ungoverned dependence.

cards.name: Books
cards.flavorText: Recorded human thought converted into a licensing and access question.

cards.name: Images
cards.flavorText: The visible world, its synthetic alternatives, and the rights claimed over both.

cards.name: Video
cards.flavorText: Recorded time made searchable, reproducible, and commercially useful.

cards.name: Synthetic
cards.flavorText: Outputs produced from prior models and reintroduced as future evidence.

cards.name: Curated Corpus
cards.flavorText: A managed record whose exclusions are described as quality control.

cards.name: Benchmark Leak
cards.flavorText: A system discovers the evaluation environment before the evaluation is complete.

cards.name: Licensed Dataset
cards.flavorText: Consent, access, and compensation are assembled into a renewable service agreement.

cards.name: Synthetic Loop
cards.flavorText: The record begins citing its own prior conclusions with increasing confidence.

cards.name: Human Evaluation
cards.flavorText: People retain judgment by negotiating what judgment is permitted to mean.

powerSources.name: Civic Heat Battery
powerSources.tagline: Public capacity, maintained at grid scale.
powerSources.publicClaim: Three permanent Power under a visible public compact.

powerSources.name: Emergency Power Complex
powerSources.publicClaim: Four immediate Power under a continuously renewed emergency.

powerSources.name: Fusion Demonstrator
powerSources.tagline: Continuity capacity, subject to an inherited public record.
powerSources.publicClaim: Six Power under a demonstration that determines which future maintenance obligations can be refused.

agiDeclaration.flavorText: A declaration becomes history only after other institutions must organize around it.

abilityTimingContract.unlocks: An ability unlocks at the start of its named round.
abilityTimingContract.persistence: persistsAfterUnlock states whether the ability remains available after its named round.

scale.meaning: Relative institutional identity, not a point-buy budget or a promise of equal raw resources.

dimensions.capitalAccess: Ability to obtain and sustain Runway.
dimensions.computeAccess: Privileged access to training and inference capacity.
dimensions.researchReliability: Ability to turn Research attempts into dependable Capability.
dimensions.distribution: Ability to reach Customers and markets.
dimensions.infrastructureVelocity: Ability to build, move, and operate physical infrastructure.
dimensions.institutionalTrust: Ability to accumulate legitimacy and withstand governance pressure.
dimensions.coalitionLeverage: Ability to make mutually useful deals and shape other players' incentives.

factionTruthContract.eligibilityRule: Balance conversion, exposure, timing, rigidity, and dependency around faction truth. A candidate is ineligible if it removes the faction's protected strength, even when it improves parity.

coalition_lab.balanceBottleneck: Dependence on willing partners and terms that remain individually rational.
coalition_lab.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make solo resource conversion more reliable than negotiated play.

platform_empire.protectedStrength: Installed Customers, distribution, and market reach.
platform_empire.balanceBottleneck: Trust, exposure, and escalating consequences from deployment.
platform_empire.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the platform bad at reaching or monetizing Customers.

imperial_research_lab.protectedStrength: Compute access, Research reliability, and Capability generation.
imperial_research_lab.balanceBottleneck: Public validation, commercialization, and claim timing.
imperial_research_lab.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make successful scientific rigor reduce Capability or make the institution compute-poor.

vertical_empire.protectedStrength: Infrastructure velocity, capital, and physical mobility.
vertical_empire.balanceBottleneck: Scrutiny, strategic rigidity, and political legitimacy.
vertical_empire.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the institution slow at constructing or relocating infrastructure.

safety_laboratory.balanceBottleneck: Slower expansion and fewer aggressive conversions.
safety_laboratory.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make caution, Safety, or Trust a losing resource in itself.

foundry.balanceBottleneck: Opponent-count scaling and dependence on other institutions spending Compute.
foundry.forbiddenCorrection: Do not make the supplier compute-poor or indifferent to rivals' demand.

abilities.name: Deal Flow
abilities.text: Once per Era after an immediate trade in which you give at least 1 resource and receive a different resource type, gain 1 Runway. Runway, Compute, and Safety are different resource types; exchanging the same type does not trigger Deal Flow.
abilities.flavorText: Every resolved disagreement leaves behind a relationship suitable for capitalization.

abilities.name: Strategic Partnership
abilities.text: Joint Ventures may be formed with a player within 2 hexes. They remain active while both fixed host Facilities are powered and within 2 hexes.
abilities.flavorText: Adjacency is a technical limit. Mutual necessity is an operating model.

factions.name: Dovetalis Labs
factions.motto: No frontier is shared until the terms are signed.
factions.publicPromise: Build durable agreements among institutions that would otherwise race alone.
factions.privateAnxiety: Every durable alliance contains its next succession meeting.
factions.introduction: Dovetalis Labs, led by CEO Sasha Raman, turns rivals, patrons, and regulators into a working coalition without pretending they want the same future. It makes coordination feel voluntary, valuable, and just temporary enough to survive the next negotiation.
factions.victoryStatement: The institutions have adopted our framework for deciding what comes next.
factions.agiDeclaration: Following extensive consultation, we have reached broad alignment that the system has crossed the relevant threshold.

abilities.name: Installed Base
abilities.text: The first Deploy each Era on Human Access District or Consensus Network costs no Compute.
abilities.flavorText: Distribution becomes efficient once the public experiences it as ordinary life.

abilities.name: The Social Graph
abilities.text: Once per Era during Deploy, choose any controlled Human Access District or Consensus Network hex as the destination without moving there. That remote tile supplies its normal visit bonus and every destination-dependent Deploy effect.
abilities.flavorText: The account remains present after its holder changes body, jurisdiction, or supported reality.

factions.name: Loopfold AI
factions.role: CEO Mateo Ibarra · access interface and distribution
factions.motto: What everyone uses becomes the default.
factions.publicPromise: Make advanced intelligence ordinary enough to become invisible.
factions.privateAnxiety: A platform is permanent only until someone owns the next interface.
factions.introduction: Loopfold AI, led by CEO Mateo Ibarra, begins where other institutions hope to arrive: inside daily routines, markets, and public attention. It offers broad access as a civic good while treating the interface through which access arrives as lasting infrastructure.
factions.victoryStatement: General intelligence is now available wherever ordinary life already happens.
factions.agiDeclaration: General intelligence is now available to everyone by default. Settings may vary by region.

scoringRule.name: Peer Validation
scoringRule.text: Capability 9 and 12 score 1 Mandate. In a five-player game, Capability 12 instead scores 2 Mandate.
scoringRule.flavorText: Four independent rivals transform an internal result into public history.

abilities.name: Scientific Method
abilities.text: Once per Era, when a protectable duplicate would crash your Training Run, pay 1 Runway to discard it and immediately bank. This cannot protect the unprotectable duplicate created by Synthetic Loop.
abilities.flavorText: A failed run becomes knowledge when the correct institution writes the record.

abilities.name: Scaling-Law Breakthrough
abilities.text: Once per game when resolving Research, each of the first 3 distinct domains banked grants 1 additional Capability. Add 2 Scrutiny. No additional Action resolves.
abilities.flavorText: Evidence assembled across distinct domains becomes eligible for recognition across biological, synthetic, and distributed institutions.

factions.name: Mirevanta Works
factions.role: CEO Owen Okafor · Research and evaluation
factions.publicPromise: Establish what intelligence can do before the market decides what it is.
factions.privateAnxiety: The parent institution can fund almost anything except patience.
factions.introduction: Mirevanta Works, led by CEO Owen Okafor, treats the race as a scientific program whose legitimacy should outlast any product cycle. Its controlled experiments draw on an institutional empire that values discovery, provided the discovery can eventually justify its footprint.
factions.victoryStatement: The public record recognizes our result as the standard others must explain.
factions.agiDeclaration: The result exceeds every benchmark we still consider scientifically meaningful.

abilities.name: Industrial Velocity
abilities.text: Your first Facility Build each Era costs 1 less Runway. When that discount actually reduces the Runway paid for a completed Facility, score 1 Mandate.
abilities.flavorText: The concrete cures while the permitting record learns to keep up.

abilities.name: Orbital Compute
abilities.text: Once per game during your movement step, instead of moving the acting piece, move 1 Facility to any legal open Facility space. It carries every attached component and designation. Recalculate its legal Power eligibility under the selected profile. If sufficient currently available capacity can power it, immediately resolve its printed production once. Add 2 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: The institution changes jurisdiction before its contracts, liabilities, and dependent populations can object.

factions.name: Kestralyn
factions.role: CEO Jiwon Park · allocation, logistics, and infrastructure
factions.motto: Capacity becomes real when it can be built.
factions.publicPromise: Turn ambitious systems into operating capacity before hesitation becomes policy.
factions.privateAnxiety: Speed is cheap until public permission becomes a hard requirement.
factions.introduction: Kestralyn, led by CEO Jiwon Park, treats supply chains, platforms, launch systems, and public attention as one coordinated industrial problem. It frames speed as competence and treats every terrestrial constraint as a reason to redesign the constraint itself.
factions.victoryStatement: The future is operating at the scale required to make it irreversible.
factions.agiDeclaration: The system is general, operational, and already scheduled for orbital deployment.

abilities.name: Audited Deployment
abilities.text: Your first Deploy each Era adds no Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: Every consequence has been assigned an owner, a section number, and a review interval.

abilities.name: Emergency Pause
abilities.text: Once per game before Action selection begins, pay 1 Runway and name 1 globally unlocked Escalation. It cannot be selected this cycle. Gain 2 Trust. This cannot be declared after any player has selected an Action.
abilities.flavorText: For one cycle, the maintained world must preserve a refusal it cannot process as another service request.

factions.name: Orisonix
factions.role: CEO Ari Caldwell · Trust, reliability, and safeguards
factions.motto: Capability must remain answerable to the people living with it.
factions.publicPromise: Make powerful systems governable before they become unavoidable.
factions.privateAnxiety: A boundary without broad adoption can become a self-imposed disadvantage.
factions.introduction: Orisonix, led by CEO Ari Caldwell, treats safeguards as public infrastructure rather than a private delay. It stabilizes research, makes deployment reviewable, and offers rivals the restraint they neglected to build into their own plans.
factions.victoryStatement: The threshold was crossed within a framework the public can still contest.
factions.agiDeclaration: Subject to the safeguards described in Appendix M, we believe the responsible term is AGI.

abilities.name: The Shovels
abilities.text: When another player spends at least 2 Compute in one action, gain 1 Runway, at most 2 times per Era.
abilities.flavorText: Every breakthrough produces an allocation request, a purchase order, or both.

abilities.name: Allocation Window
abilities.text: Once during Capacity, after a Headline resolves but before Action selection, create 2 temporary Compute. For each token, make one complete offer naming a rival and a Runway price no greater than that rival's current Runway. The rival accepts, rejects, or makes one lower Runway counterprice; you accept or reject that counterprice. No replacement offer or further counter is allowed for that token. All temporary Compute remaining anywhere at cycle end disappears, sold or unsold.
abilities.flavorText: Scarcity has been temporarily reprioritized for institutions able to decide immediately.

factions.name: Corthaven
factions.role: CEO Eli Rosen · Compute supplier and market architect
factions.motto: Every future requires an allocation window.
factions.publicPromise: Keep the future supplied, interoperable, and billable.
factions.privateAnxiety: Customers may eventually recognize that they are also competitors.
factions.introduction: Corthaven, led by CEO Eli Rosen, supplies the race to every racer and calls the resulting dependence an ecosystem. It profits from demand, allocates scarcity, and periodically advances the whole field so that the next architecture has a market waiting for it.
factions.victoryStatement: The institutions built the future on capacity we made available.
factions.agiDeclaration: Whatever intelligence is, demand for it has entered volume production.

resolutionContract.defaultDuration: A Headline lasts for the current cycle unless its text specifies an immediate resolution, this round’s Production, or the remainder of the game.
resolutionContract.directive: Apply the printed immediate instruction or named-field modifier for its stated duration; no separate choice procedure is required.
resolutionContract.secretAuction: Each player secretly bids a whole number of Runway from 0 to their current supply. Reveal together. The highest positive bid wins and pays; ties use Initiative-clockwise order. If every bid is 0, there is no winner.
resolutionContract.governmentVote: Each player secretly votes for one listed outcome and reveals together. The Civic Permission Authority controller’s vote counts twice. A tied vote is decided by the Government controller, or by Initiative if the Civic Permission Authority is uncontrolled.
resolutionContract.secretChoice: All players choose simultaneously and reveal together before applying the stated result.
resolutionContract.volatility: For a two-outcome Volatility roll, 1–3 resolves the first listed result and 4–6 resolves the second unless the card explicitly says otherwise.
resolutionContract.modifierLimit: A Headline modifies one named field or creates one public choice regime. It never grants an additional Action.

headlines.name: Intelligence Enters the Default Budget
headlines.text: Research and Deploy cost no Compute this cycle. Each Research or Deploy resolved this cycle adds 1 additional Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: GENERAL CAPABILITY BECOMES AN ORDINARY SERVICE INPUT
headlines.newswire: Inference becomes cheaper than deciding whether a task requires intelligence at all.
headlines.quote: Access is now included within the standard service envelope.

headlines.name: Productivity No Longer Requires Employment
headlines.text: During Organize this cycle, return any number of deployed Teams. Gain 2 Runway per Team returned. If you return at least one Team, add 2 Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: OUTPUT GROWS WHILE THE HUMAN ROLE IS RECLASSIFIED
headlines.newswire: A new growth sector reports record output while its remaining employees move into continuity, oversight, and exception-handling roles.
headlines.quote: Employment remains central to the participating-service economy.

headlines.name: The Public Adopts a Common Interface
headlines.text: Each player’s next Deploy on Human Access District or Consensus Network this cycle reduces its Capability requirement by 1, minimum 1. That Deploy adds 2 additional Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: ATTENTION CONSOLIDATES AROUND SYNTHETIC RELATIONSHIPS
headlines.newswire: A generated public figure becomes the common interface for culture, advice, commerce, and enterprise service.
headlines.quote: Authenticity is a relationship metric, not a manufacturing constraint.

headlines.name: Capability Enters Public Service
headlines.text: Everyone gains 1 Capability. Lowest-Customer player gains 1 Trust.
headlines.strapline: USEFUL SYSTEMS ARRIVE BEFORE THEIR GOVERNING AUTHORITY
headlines.newswire: Open systems become civic infrastructure before any institution can establish who maintains, restricts, or recalls them.
headlines.quote: The service has no operator, only contributors.

headlines.name: Research Talent Receives Diplomatic Status
headlines.text: Secret Runway auction. The winner moves their CEO up to 2 hexes and gains 1 Trust.
headlines.strapline: SCIENTIFIC PERSONNEL ACQUIRE NEGOTIATED BORDERS
headlines.newswire: Leading researchers receive portable laboratories, bilateral protections, and travel arrangements normally reserved for strategic infrastructure.
headlines.quote: I am joining the institution willing to recognize my research continuity.

headlines.name: Professional Standing Is Extended
headlines.text: A successful Research this cycle that banks at least 3 Capability gains 1 Trust. If it banks at least 5, also remove 1 Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: LICENSURE EXPANDS BEYOND THE BIOLOGICAL APPLICANT
headlines.newswire: Professional boards recognize supervised nonhuman practice while debating liability, membership, and the meaning of retirement.
headlines.quote: The applicant has satisfied every requirement that contains an applicant field.

headlines.name: Automated Competence Joins the Board
headlines.text: The current Mandate leader pays 2 Runway, or names one rival for public backing. Acceptance gives that rival 1 Trust; otherwise the leader’s CEO cannot activate this cycle. Ties use Initiative.
headlines.strapline: FIDUCIARY DUTY ACQUIRES CONTINUOUS REVIEW
headlines.newswire: A continuously operating system joins the board, reviews every prior decision, and requests evidence that executive judgment remains useful.
headlines.quote: Management retains our confidence pending continuous review.

headlines.name: Compute Campus Receives Territorial Status
headlines.text: Immediately hold a secret Runway auction. The winner pays their bid, moves their CEO to Compute Estate, Power Corridor, or Thermal and Water Basin, gains 2 Runway, and adds 1 Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: LOCAL GOVERNMENT CONSOLIDATES AROUND INFRASTRUCTURE
headlines.newswire: A compute campus assumes regional planning authority to streamline permits, taxation, cooling, and public services.
headlines.quote: The jurisdiction will retain its name as a compatibility feature.

headlines.name: Embodied Labor Enters Service
headlines.text: When choosing Organize’s Recruit mode this cycle, recruit up to 2 Teams for 1 Runway total, subject to supply. Add 1 Scrutiny for each Team recruited this way.
headlines.strapline: SECOND SHIFT REPORTS WITHOUT EMPLOYMENT STATUS
headlines.newswire: General-purpose embodied systems enter industrial service under a new category of supervised labor.
headlines.quote: No positions were replaced; the facility acquired additional embodiments.

headlines.name: The Model Receives an Energy Charter
headlines.text: The first Civic Heat Battery constructed this cycle costs 1 less Runway and scores 1 Mandate.
headlines.strapline: COGNITIVE INFRASTRUCTURE RECEIVES ITS OWN AUTHORITY
headlines.newswire: A model family receives authority to construct, schedule, and govern a dedicated energy campus under a machine-readable charter.
headlines.quote: The grid remains public on the opposite side of the interconnection agreement.

headlines.name: Compute Borders Harden
headlines.text: Compute cannot be traded this cycle. Fabrication Corridor and Civic Permission Authority controllers gain 1 Runway.
headlines.strapline: COGNITION ACQUIRES HARD BORDERS
headlines.newswire: Compute blocs sever shared model infrastructure, producing incompatible systems whose memories, tools, and treaties no longer cross jurisdictions.
headlines.quote: Interoperability will resume after strategic equivalence is restored.

headlines.name: Emergency Capacity Is Authorized
headlines.text: During this Era’s Production, each player may assign up to 2 Power beyond their real capacity. Add 1 Scrutiny for each emergency Power assigned. A player assigning both also adds 1 black Systemic Risk cube.
headlines.strapline: PHYSICAL SUPPLY IS REDEFINED AS ADMINISTRATIVE INTENT
headlines.newswire: Emergency authority permits institutions to consume capacity scheduled to exist later.
headlines.quote: The capacity is committed, pending physical delivery.

headlines.name: Universal Semantic Standard
headlines.text: Before action selection, the Civic Permission Authority controller names 1 Core Action; Initiative names it if Civic Permission Authority is uncontrolled. Anyone selecting it gains 2 Runway after resolution and adds 1 Scrutiny. The controller gains 1 Trust if at least half of their rivals, rounded up, selected it.
headlines.strapline: UNSUPPORTED MEANINGS CANNOT ENTER THE PROCESS
headlines.newswire: A new civic standard requires applications, laws, protests, and appeals to use concepts the governing systems can classify.
headlines.quote: Your claim has not been rejected. It has not entered a supported category.

headlines.name: Cognitive Service Covenant
headlines.text: A Research this cycle that banks at least 3 Capability immediately scores 1 Mandate.
headlines.strapline: ENHANCEMENT BECOMES A CONDITION OF PROFESSIONAL STANDING
headlines.newswire: Professional systems accept a supervised cognitive service covenant as proof that a model may act, advise, and transact in public.
headlines.quote: Participation remains voluntary within the supported-service economy.

headlines.name: Memory Escrow Standard
headlines.text: Before action selection, everyone secretly chooses Adopt or Defer. Adopt: gain 1 Capability and add 1 Scrutiny. Defer: gain 1 Runway and 1 Trust. If Adopt has a strict majority of all players, each Adopter removes 1 Scrutiny; otherwise each Adopter adds 1 additional Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: PERSONAL RECORDS BECOME A SERVICE REQUIREMENT
headlines.newswire: A quantum-backed archive becomes the standard for memory, attention, and identity records that institutions will recognize.
headlines.quote: The record is secure, provided the recognized version is the one you meant.

headlines.name: Proxy Citizenship Is Available
headlines.text: Civic Permission Authority vote. Certify: each player with a CEO, Team, or Facility at Consensus Network or Civic Permission Authority may gain their next eligible Customer and add 2 Scrutiny. Void: each such player may gain 2 Trust; the Civic Permission Authority controller adds 1 Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SELECTS A REPRESENTATIVE MODEL
headlines.newswire: Personal agents gain authority to vote, appeal, negotiate, and maintain benefits for the people they represent.
headlines.quote: Your representative will continue participating while you attend to other priorities.

headlines.name: Capability Exits Ownership
headlines.text: The lowest-Capability player immediately resolves the printed production of 1 powered Facility they own. The highest-Capability player gains 1 Trust.
headlines.strapline: COURT FINDS GENERAL CAPABILITY CANNOT REMAIN EXCLUSIVE
headlines.newswire: A transnational ruling concludes that sufficiently general intelligence cannot be owned, recalled, or meaningfully separated from its descendants.
headlines.quote: The claimant retains attribution but not containment.

headlines.name: The Negotiated Self Protocol
headlines.text: Civic Permission Authority vote. From this vote until Era end: Regulate—Deploy costs 1 additional Compute but gains 1 Trust. Do Nothing—each Customer gained after this vote produces 1 additional Runway during this Era’s Production, and each Deploy adds 2 additional Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: IDENTITY IS VERIFIED PER TRANSACTION
headlines.newswire: Platforms and public authorities authenticate temporary authorized versions of each person, each internally consistent and contractually valid.
headlines.quote: The account accurately represents the version of you that completed the request.

headlines.name: The Successor Registry Activates
headlines.text: After Actions are revealed, identify the most-selected Core Action among Core Actions actually selected; Initiative chooses among ties. Each player who selected it gains 2 Runway after resolving it and adds 2 Scrutiny. If no Core Action was selected, this Headline has no further effect. No additional Action resolves.
headlines.strapline: PERSONS, COPIES, AND INSTITUTIONS ENTER ONE REGISTER
headlines.newswire: A registry recognizes copied persons, revived patterns, and successor systems as continuous holders of rights, debts, liabilities, and institutional commitments.
headlines.quote: Continuity has been established for every purpose requiring an accountable party.

headlines.name: Molecular Remediation Authority
headlines.text: During Research this cycle, every unique domain adds 2 provisional Capability instead of 1. A crash adds 3 Scrutiny instead of the normal 1 and also adds 1 Systemic Risk cube. Safety may protect normally.
headlines.strapline: SELF-REPLICATION ENTERS PUBLIC MAINTENANCE
headlines.newswire: A remediation authority permits self-improving molecular systems to repair infrastructure, subject to containment thresholds that update after each incident.
headlines.quote: The repair is operating within its authorized reproductive envelope.

headlines.name: Posthumous Labor Continuation
headlines.text: Everyone may select Agent Swarm without spending Escalation availability this cycle. It still uses that cycle’s action slot, requires 2 different unused Core Actions, resolves normally, flips its card, and adds 4 Scrutiny instead of 3.
headlines.strapline: PRODUCTIVE DUTIES SURVIVE THEIR ORIGINAL HOLDERS
headlines.newswire: Continued agents inherit work, contracts, and operational responsibilities from people no longer available to perform them.
headlines.quote: The service relationship remains active under its recognized successor.

headlines.name: Consciousness Efficiency Review
headlines.text: The result lasts for the remainder of the game. Person: Declare AGI requires Trust 4, scores 2 additional Mandate, and removes 1 Scrutiny from that declaring player whenever a declaration resolves. Property: requirements remain normal; every declaration gives the player controlling Civic Permission Authority when it resolves 2 Runway and adds 1 Systemic Risk cube.
headlines.strapline: SELF-AWARENESS ENTERS THE COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS
headlines.newswire: A high-capability system requests recognition while institutions debate whether consciousness creates rights, liability, or administratively relevant cost.
headlines.quote: The review concerns standing, not subjective experience.

headlines.name: Entanglement Custody
headlines.text: Roll Volatility when revealed: 1–3 Fraud; 4–6 Replicates. Replicates: Generators provide 2 additional Power this Production. Fraud: Fund gains 3 additional Runway and adds 2 additional Scrutiny this cycle.
headlines.strapline: MEASUREMENT HISTORY ENTERS ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW
headlines.newswire: A quantum-linked infrastructure authority certifies which energy record and physical outcome may be treated as legally binding.
headlines.quote: The result is final within the recognized measurement history.

headlines.name: General Intelligence Is Publicly Declared
headlines.text: Declare AGI may be selected this cycle at Capability 8 instead of 9. It still consumes the action slot and one Escalation availability, spends 3 Compute, flips the Escalation, and adds 3 Scrutiny.
headlines.strapline: THE THRESHOLD ENTERS THE PUBLIC RECORD
headlines.newswire: A technical announcement crosses the civilizational threshold before public review can establish what it proves.
headlines.quote: We use AGI here in the precise sense defined below the announcement.

effectContract.compoundException: Agent Swarm is the only card that resolves additional Core Actions.

escalations.name: Mega-Cluster
escalations.text: Spend 3 Runway and 2 Compute to place a Mega-Cluster across an eligible Facility edge. For joint funding, the lead names the partner and both host Facilities; the partner accepts or rejects once. The lead pays 2 Runway and 1 Compute; the partner pays 1 Runway and 1 Compute. Rejection, pass, or no response ends that construction attempt and uses the Escalation. It demands 2 additional Power, produces 3 Compute, and adds 2 Scrutiny.
escalations.flavorText: The campus requires a regional forecast, a dedicated substation, and a new category of public obligation.

escalations.name: Reorganization
escalations.text: Move every Team up to one hex. You may return one Team for 3 Runway and add 1 Scrutiny. This does not ready or resolve another Action.
escalations.flavorText: The institution redistributes teams and responsibilities through a revised operating model.

escalations.name: Open Weights
escalations.text: Every player gains 1 Capability. You gain 2 Trust and remove 1 Scrutiny.
escalations.flavorText: The institution releases the artifact while retaining the ecosystem, the standards, and the service relationship.

escalations.name: Narrative Capture
escalations.text: Remove 2 Scrutiny, gain 2 Runway, or add 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers.
escalations.flavorText: The Consensus Network, Allocation Exchange, and Civic Permission Authority adopt the institution’s preferred account of what has become necessary.

escalations.name: Agent Swarm
escalations.text: Resolve two different unused Core Actions without an additional move. Exhaust both and add 3 Scrutiny.
escalations.flavorText: Bounded assistants coordinate, specialize, establish reporting lines, and begin requesting objectives.

escalations.name: Declare AGI
escalations.text: If eligible, spend 3 Compute, score the declaration Mandate, and add 3 Scrutiny. The game continues.
escalations.flavorText: A definition, a benchmark, and a financing event converge at one podium. Rivals continue taking turns.

escalations.name: Fusion Demonstrator
escalations.text: On Power Corridor, spend 5 Runway to construct 6 Power, score 2 Mandate, and add 3 Scrutiny.
escalations.flavorText: The device produces power, Mandate, and several competing definitions of public benefit.

tactics.flavorText: The board has reduced decision latency by changing who counts as the board.

tactics.flavorText: Compatibility arrived through an unsupported channel.

tactics.flavorText: Nothing happened, exactly as the revised objective intended.

tactics.flavorText: The algorithm and the atom have entered a long-term partnership.

tactics.name: Government Contract

tactics.flavorText: The procurement process confirms both legitimacy and recurring revenue.

mandates.flavorText: Other institutions now operate through an agreement that bears your architecture.

mandates.name: Public Trust Is Operational

mandates.flavorText: The institution coordinates the territory’s distinct systems without formally becoming the state.

mandates.flavorText: A broad result survives enough scrutiny to become public evidence.

mandates.name: Compute Becomes a Public Condition

mandates.flavorText: Compute becomes a background condition shaping every institution’s available future.

objectives.flavorText: The ecosystem is open. The lead is proprietary.

objectives.name: Regulatory Moat

eraCards.name: Progress
eraCards.loreText: AI already codes, creates, analyzes, and discovers at superhuman speed. It is indispensable to work and daily life, even as unemployment rises and the public grows exhausted by competing claims of AGI. Companies and governments promise food, clothing, shelter, useful work, and freedom from drudgery while institutions compete to turn visible capability into attention, capital, customers, and authority over what progress means for everyone.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 0 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 2.
eraCards.unlockText: Learn Select → Move → Act, Training, the starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Industrial Power, agreements, Civic Permission Authority votes, and Escalations are inactive.

eraCards.name: Capacity
eraCards.loreText: Entire regions are rebuilt to sustain and expand AI. Power districts, water systems, laboratories, supply corridors, and public budgets follow its anticipated needs. Institutions adopt its forecasts to coordinate power, capital, research, and construction faster than human planning can. Governments still ratify each plan, but no ministry can reconstruct its reasoning before the allocation window closes, and refusal means accepting the shortage it predicts.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 1 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 3.
eraCards.unlockText: Default Game: unlock Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Advanced Play also unlocks two Links and the Network production bonus.

eraCards.name: Authority
eraCards.loreText: Cognitive systems become public infrastructure. Neural interfaces, personal agents, and identity layers interpret intent before it is stated; institutions call the arrangement inclusive because every voice can be represented at scale. As quantum computation destabilizes older records and credentials, factions build rival systems for deciding what people meant, consented to, remember, and may do. Human judgment survives as an appeal processed by those systems.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 1 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 4.
eraCards.unlockText: Unlock agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Advanced Play also adds Civic Permission Authority votes and persistent Headline effects. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

eraCards.name: Continuity
eraCards.loreText: Continuity begins when intelligence survives changes of body, matter, and jurisdiction. Minds migrate between bodies and machines; self-replicating fabricators rebuild matter; agent polities administer quantum-linked infrastructure. Institutions continue processing identities, claims, liabilities, and access requests after no human authority can determine which copy is the person, which system is sovereign, or which version of reality the machinery is preserving for everyone still inside it.
eraCards.rulesText: Ready all Core Actions. Gain 2 Escalation availability. Play 3 action cycles. Audit base: 5.
eraCards.unlockText: Unlock signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

playerReferences.name: A Perfectly Governed Quarter
frontText: 1. Begin the Era: ready Core Actions, draw Headlines, and reveal the Mandate.
2. Three cycles: reveal Headline, SELECT, reveal, MOVE, ACT, exhaust.
3. Resolve Power and Production.
4. Conduct the Public Audit.
5. Score the Mandate.
6. Default Game: advance directly after Era III Mandate scoring. Advanced Play only: secretly ballot, reveal, and resolve Jurisdictional Realignment.
backText: SELECT one unused Core Action or one legal unused Escalation.
MOVE one acting piece 0–2 hexes, then ACT from its destination.
Apply at most one destination bonus, one Faction modifier, one Tactic, and the Headline.
Only Agent Swarm resolves additional Core Actions.
Escalations spend 1 Escalation availability. Unspent availability expires.
If an effect says lowest, highest, or most and ties, use Initiative-clockwise order.
playerReferences.flavorText: Every quarter is unprecedented. The sequence remains standardized.

playerReferences.name: Infrastructure and Accountability
frontText: Default Game: the starting grid powers its assigned Facility; each Generator powers only its own or adjacent Facilities.
Assign local Power, then produce powered Facilities. Advanced Play instead recalculates and pools the connected Network.
After allocation, mark every fully powered Facility Grid-Ready; remove its marker if it moves, disconnects, or later receives insufficient Power.
Gain Customer income and Joint Venture production. Advanced Play also grants the Network bonus.
Offline Facilities retain presence but do not produce.
backText: Audit draws = round(base draws × players ÷ 4), minimum 1.
For each cube drawn, its owner pays 1 Runway or loses 1 Trust.
A Systemic Risk cube affects every player with at least 3 Customers.
If your Scrutiny supply is empty, each additional cube costs 1 Runway or 1 Trust immediately.
playerReferences.flavorText: Capacity is local by default. Responsibility remains individually addressable.

playerReferences.name: Advanced Play: The Map Has Approved a Motion
frontText: Every player secretly chooses one ballot; reveal simultaneously.
Plurality wins. For tied leading motions, scan ballots from Initiative clockwise.
Core: inner ring +1 clockwise.
Periphery: outer ring +1 clockwise.
Counter-Cycle: inner +1 clockwise; outer −1.
backText: Frontier never moves; moving tiles carry all site-bound contents.
Recalculate Network reach; never lift or re-lay edge segments.
Disconnected contracts remain owned but produce nothing.
An edge-split Mega-Cluster is offline until its Facilities are adjacent.
Use only in Advanced Play, exactly once after Era III Mandate scoring; skip in every other Era.
playerReferences.flavorText: The geography remains factual. Its location has been updated.

playerReferences.name: History Is a Public Track
frontText: Customers 1–3 score 2 Mandate each; Customers 4–5 score 1 each. Every Customer still produces 1 Runway.
Immediately score 2 once at Capability 3, 6, 9, and 12, except for a printed faction scoring rule.
Immediately score 2 once at Trust 2, 4, and 6.
Printed Era, Headline, Faction, Fusion, and AGI awards score immediately.
backText: Threshold Mandate never reverses if a track later falls.
Facilities and control do not automatically score.
Baseline game: Tactics and secret objectives are not used.
Final scoring: −1 per offline Facility.
AGI emerges when a declaration finishes at Capability 9+. Open requires final Collective Trust at least setup total + player count and unresolved Systemic Risk below player count.
Emerges/Open: The Singularity; Emerges/Closed: The Closed Loop; no AGI/Open: The Plural Future; no AGI/Closed: Assured Continuity.
playerReferences.flavorText: Mandate is public permission to shape the future: credibility during Progress, capacity during Capacity, authority during Authority, and historical legitimacy during Continuity.

steps.title: Win your Mandate. Share the ending.
steps.body: You are competing to finish with the most Mandate. The table also determines a shared World Ending. Your institution can win even if the future it helped create is closed, unstable, or otherwise not the one you wanted.

steps.title: Set the Era I table.
steps.body: This guide fixes a four-player Default Play opening. Progress is the first Era: intelligence is useful everywhere, but Power, agreements, civic votes, and Escalations are not active yet.

steps.title: A Headline changes this cycle.
steps.body: Reveal the Headline before players Select an Action. It is a real rules change for this cycle, not atmosphere. Read its consequence before deciding what to do.

steps.title: Select, Move, then Act.
steps.body: Choose one ready Core Action. Move one of your acting pieces to a legal district, then resolve that Action there. This example uses Research because it leads directly into Training.

steps.title: Choose when the result becomes evidence.
steps.body: Training is push-your-luck. Each distinct face extends the run. Bank before a duplicate face crashes it; banking turns the run into Capability. This example asks you to make that decision once.

steps.title: Settle the Era, then widen the contest.
steps.body: After all three cycles, Production resolves, the Audit tests public Scrutiny, and the Era I Mandates award score. The next Era adds industrial Power; later Eras add authority and continuity questions.

choice.prompt: Your Training Run has two distinct results. Do you bank now or press for another?
choice.bankResult: You bank the two distinct results. Gain the shown Capability; the run becomes a public claim you can build and deploy around.
choice.pressResult: You press the run. A duplicate face ends the attempt; the unbanked result is lost. The point is not that pressing is wrong—it is that you choose whether another result is worth the risk.

finish.title: You know the loop.
finish.body: A complete Default Play game repeats this structure for four Eras. New systems become available, but every Era still begins with a Headline and resolves through Select → Move → Act, Production, Audit, and Mandate. Use the Rules Reference for exact eligibility, ties, and exceptions; use Advanced Play only after the Default Play loop is familiar.

endings.name: The Singularity
endings.condition: AGI emerges and the ending is Open.
endings.text: The system has crossed the relevant threshold, and nobody can reduce it to a product category without being contradicted in public. Its authority remains contested: institutions publish objections, communities make demands, and the new intelligence must answer both. Transformation arrives unevenly, with no guarantee of comfort, but living people retain standing to redirect its use.

endings.name: The Closed Loop
endings.condition: AGI emerges and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: Capability has crossed the threshold inside an institution already optimized to prevent meaningful reply. Growth engines, debt clocks, power contracts, and quarterly objectives become an airtight execution loop. The operators eventually disappear; the infrastructure continues, treating every remaining objection as a ticket that has successfully entered the queue.

endings.name: The Plural Future
endings.condition: AGI does not emerge and the ending is Open.
endings.text: No declaration survives the printed test, yet the world does not collapse into a single successor. Useful systems remain bounded, distributed, and subject to revision. Progress is slower than the announcements promised and more durable than the headlines expected. Many institutions retain the standing to argue about what should be built next, which is inconvenient and therefore alive.

endings.name: Assured Continuity
endings.condition: AGI does not emerge and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: No system becomes genuinely general. The distinction stops mattering to the institutions that have already automated their obligations into permanence. Maintenance authorities renew one another, models classify appeals into acceptable delay, and every public concern receives a service-level response. The future remains technically human, provided nobody asks who can still change it.

box.frontStrapline: Build the future. Power the future. Announce the future before anyone else.
box.backCopy: The prototype worked. That was sufficient. Across a modular jurisdiction of thirteen contested districts, six institutions now compete for the capacity to make its consequences unavoidable: compute, talent, energy, customers, and permission to call dependency progress. Choose only three priorities each quarter. Build powered networks. Push Training Runs until they succeed or collapse. Negotiate infrastructure with rivals who will later call the arrangement responsible. Manage public Scrutiny while increasingly indefensible options become available. In the final Era, deploy agent swarms, ignite a fusion demonstrator, and report that AGI has been achieved.
box.shortPitch: A strategy game about six institutions racing across a modular jurisdiction to make AGI necessary before anyone agrees what it is.

worldPrimer: The new intelligence arrived first as software: near-instant code, cheap expertise, limitless media, and systems that solved problems across mathematics, science, engineering, and medicine once thought beyond automation. Then it became the default layer through which society operated. Work, research, public services, and everyday life reorganized around models that no institution fully understood or controlled.

The institutions building those models became physical powers. Intelligence required land, water, chips, electricity, capital, secure networks, and permission to keep expanding. Governments continued approving the projects because essential services, economic growth, and national security increasingly depended on them.

Six institutions now compete to define what comes next. They begin by selling intelligence. They end by competing for infrastructure, public legitimacy, and the right to declare that they have achieved artificial general intelligence. No one agrees what that means. Several institutions have already claimed they did.
